Download the ZIP for Windows, macOS or Linux and unzip it to run. You can also install with one terminal line; after that the app updates itself (see Updates).
Which file to download
OS Download (latest version) Run
Windows 10/11 Chickxel-windows-x64.zip Unzip and double-click Chickxel.exe
macOS 12 or later, Apple Silicon (M1 and later) Chickxel-macos-arm64.zip Unzip, move Chickxel.app to the Applications folder, then double-click it
macOS 12 or later, Intel Chickxel-macos-x64.zip Same as above
Linux, x64 (Intel or AMD) Chickxel-linux-x64.zip Unzip and run Chickxel. If it doesn't start, turn on Allow executing file as program in its properties, or run chmod +x Chickxel
Linux, ARM64 Chickxel-linux-arm64.zip Same as above
Your Mac's chip is shown in Apple menu → About This Mac. On Linux, uname -m prints x86_64 for x64 and aarch64 for ARM64. Changes are listed on the releases page.
Installing from the terminal
macOS and Linux — paste the line below into a terminal to download the build for your CPU, install it and launch it. macOS installs to /Applications/Chickxel.app; Linux installs to ~/.local/share/Chickxel and adds it to the applications menu (no sudo needed).
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/1000Pro-1997/Chickxel/main/install.sh | sh
Windows — paste the line below into PowerShell to install to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Chickxel with a Start menu shortcut. This way the 'Windows protected your PC' prompt doesn't appear.
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/1000Pro-1997/Chickxel/main/install.ps1 | iex

macOS: the associations work once Chickxel.app is in the Applications folder. If another app opens these files, choose Chickxel in the file's Open With setting.
Linux: file associations and Open in Chickxel links aren't available yet.

On Windows and macOS, you need to get past your operating system's security warning the first time (Linux shows no warning). Once the app starts, the start screen appears with no document open; choose the folder or Unity project you want to work in.
Getting past the security warning
The app isn't developer-signed, so Windows and macOS show a warning the first time.
Windows "Windows protected your PC": More info → Run anyway.
macOS "unidentified developer": right-click → Open on Chickxel.app. If that doesn't work, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway.
Linux: there's no warning. If it doesn't start, turn on Allow executing file as program in the file's properties, or run chmod +x Chickxel in a terminal.
The homepage download button opens the illustrated download guide. On Windows, open the ZIP file's Properties and select Unblock before extracting to avoid the protected-PC warning. If Edge stops the download as 'not commonly downloaded', choose More options → Keep → Show more → Keep anyway. PCs with Smart App Control enabled may block the app without offering a Run button.

When Chickxel goes online
When Where and what
At startup and Check for updates… Asks GitHub for the latest version and its changes. The automatic check can be turned off (below).
When you open the Palette web (Lospec) window Downloads palette lists and sample images from lospec.com. Favorite palettes are stored only on your computer.

When you use the Chickxel account, gallery or asset uploads Signs in to chickxel.com and uploads the picture or asset you chose (plus the editable .chickxel file if you turn that on when uploading to the gallery). Just starting the app doesn't connect (see Chickxel account).

When you click links such as the website, Discord or support Opens the address in your default browser.
The connection AI tools use to control Chickxel (MCP) is opened only on this computer (127.0.0.1) and can't be reached from outside.
Discord activity status only goes to the Discord app running on this computer. Your profile shows just the chick picture, "Playing Chickxel" and the elapsed time; nothing about your work is sent. Your account level rises as you share pictures and assets on chickxel.com and stay active. Read this page to see how to earn XP (experience points) or what the Lv badge next to your name means.
Earning XP
You earn XP for each of these activities.
How XP
Upload a picture to the gallery +10
Also share the editable .chickxel file with the picture +5
Publish a new asset package +10
Upload a new version of a published package +1
Each like from someone else on your art or assets +2
Like someone else's art or assets (3 a day count) +1
Daily check-in (your first app start or site visit of the day) +10
Each hour the app is open while you're signed in +1
You get the check-in the first time each day you start the app or visit chickxel.com while signed in. The status bar shows "Daily check-in +10 XP".
App time counts only while you're signed in. Even on several computers you get it once an hour.
A new day starts at 00:00 UTC (09:00 in Korea).
Levels and badges
Each level needs 1 XP more than the one before. Level 2 starts at 10 XP, level 3 at 21 XP and level 100 at 5,841 XP; there's no maximum level.
The badge color depends on your level.
Level Default level badge
1–4 Dim gray
5–9 Bronze
10–19 Silver
20–29 Gold
30–49 Cyan-to-purple crystal
50+ Rainbow
The badge appears on the account button and window, in the Upload to Gallery window, next to authors in the Asset Manager, and next to names on chickxel.com. Hover over it to see the level and how to earn XP.
Good to know
When you level up, the status bar shows "Level up! Lv N".
Moving badges are badge looks from level rewards. The default badge doesn't move.
If the server doesn't report a level (an older server, for example), there's no badge.
If a like is withdrawn, or a picture or asset package is deleted (by you, an admin or a report), the XP it earned (likes included) is removed. Its storage quota comes back right away.
Deleted pictures and assets stay on the server, so an admin can restore them.

pages.text:
Each level from 2 to 100 unlocks one reward that decorates your profile (99 in all). Rewards come in six slots, and you wear one per slot.
Reward slots
Slot Where and how it shows
Title (9) Text under your name by the large picture. Higher levels get rarer colors; from level 71 they flow in rainbow colors.
Level badge (20) The look of the badge next to your name, moving with flowing colors, glowing borders, sparkles or embers.
Frame (30) A pixel frame around your picture: a small look on small pictures, and a larger look with ornaments such as wings or crowns on large pictures (the account window and your site profile).
Effect (20) An animation around the large picture (sparkle dust, petals, fireflies, planets, runes and more).
Card (10) An animated background for your profile header (the top of the account window and your site profile).
Nickname effect (10) Colors and motion for the letters of your name (neon, wave, glitch, fire, galaxy, rainbow and more). The text keeps its width.
Choosing rewards
Click Change… in the account window, or use the account menu on chickxel.com, to open the level rewards page.
Click a reward or None in any slot. It changes right away and looks the same wherever your name appears in the app and on the site.
Every slot is on Auto by default: it wears the highest-level reward you've unlocked and switches by itself as you level up.
Good to know
When you unlock a reward, the badge on the account button sparkles and Manage Account… in the account menu shows how many you haven't seen (2 new). Opening the account window marks them as seen.
If your level drops because something you shared was deleted, that level's rewards lock again and slots that had one chosen go back to Auto.
Finishing the Levels tutorial gives you the title Pixel Sprout and the frame Sprout Frame at any level. Auto treats them as the lowest rewards.

Modes
Mode Result
As layers One layer per image file; a .chickxel comes in whole with its layer tree and skins (first file on top)
Under one layer One empty layer with a child layer per file (sizes kept). If a .chickxel has a layer with children, they go under its first parent.
As skins One skin per file on a single layer (skin name = file name), for tile or item variants swapped in one spot.
As frames Frames appended in file order.
Layer trees, skins, effects and tags in .chickxel files carry over in every mode. The result is saved as <name>.chickxel in the first file's folder and opened. If that name is taken, nothing is merged and you're told.

Rule Color it picks
Nearest color The most similar color by color distance. Pick RGB (redmean), OKLab or CIEDE2000 in Color distance right below; the last two are closer to how differences look.
Brightness order Ranks the image's colors by lightness and spreads them over the palette sorted by lightness, so light and dark survive even with different hues.

Hue first Among the closest hues, the closest lightness. Grays stay gray.
Lightness only The closest lightness, ignoring hue. Suits black-and-white or 4-color Game Boy-style palettes.
Brightness order and palette order rank all target cels together, so a color maps the same way in every frame.

Use this table when naming tags. For each state the leftmost name is tried first, then the next.
State Names tried (first to last)
Top-down idle idle (idle_down if there is none for the facing)
Top-down moving walk → run → the idle names
Platformer idle idle
Run run → walk → idle
Jump (rising) jump → fall → idle
Fall fall → jump → idle
Climbing a ladder climb → idle
Hanging on a ladder hang → climb → idle
Climbing a wall wall_climb → climb → idle
Hanging on a wall wall_hang → wall_climb → hang → climb → idle
Names with a direction
Add a direction to a name (walk_left) to use it when facing that way. If you drew only one side, the other side is flipped from it.
Top-down: _down, _up, _left, _right
Platformer: _left, _right

If no name matches, the first animation plays; with no animations, the first cell shows as a still picture.
Ladders add the names climb and hang; wall climbing adds wall_climb and wall_hang.
If a climbing animation stands in for a missing hang, it stays paused while the character hangs.
When flipped, the character turns around in place instead of jumping sideways.
These names also appear in the suggestions when you name a tag.

Good to know
Every edit is a single undo step. Press Esc to cancel while dragging.
You can't delete every frame or layer, and layers are deleted with their children.
A dragged layer moves within the same parent. Every 20 px you drag left takes it one level out of its parent.
Holding Alt when you drop copies too. Starting the drag with Ctrl held copies from the start.
Cels can't move to rows of a different size or type.
When pasting, cels overwrite starting at the clicked cell, frames go after the selected frame, and layers go above the original.
Cels picked across gaps can't be copied.
Cels copied from a document with a different canvas size also paste into normal layers, aligned to the top left; parts past the canvas are kept as outside-canvas artwork. Layers with their own size need the same size.
New layers made by copying get their trailing number raised by 1 (item_1 → item_2, or _1 if there's no number). Duplicate in the layer menu does the same.
Linked copies and images-only copies

Pasted into the same row, cels join the original link group and take its color.

Nesting layers and Add skin
To put a layer inside another, drag its name, hold Shift and drop it on that layer's row. An indented blue gap shows where it will land, and a not-allowed cursor shows where you can't drop.

The layer's right-click Add skin adds a blank skin or one copied from the current art; with children, With children… makes a same-named skin on all descendants too (see Layer tree and Skins).

Selecting frames 1–4 and creating a tag from the right-click menu, then dragging the end of the tag box to change its range and playing it
A tag is a named frame range that groups an animation (for example idle or run). Tags set the preview playback range, the GIF range, and export cell names and file splits.
Creating a tag
Frames 5 and 6 selected, Create tag in the frame header menu
① Selected frames 5–6 · ② Create tag…
New tag dialog: name hit, frames 5–6, direction Forward, Loop, color
③ Name · ④ Frame range · ⑤ Direction and loop · ⑥ Color
① Select a range of frames and choose ② Create tag from the right-click menu. In the dialog, set the ③ name, ④ frame range, ⑤ playback direction and loop, and ⑥ color.
Field Meaning (initial value)
③ Name The tag name; it can't be empty or match another tag. Names such as idle_down, walk_left, run, jump and fall are suggested (initially the first unused one).
④ Frames Start and end frame (inclusive); the end can't come before the start (initially the selected range).
⑤ Direction Forward, Reverse or Ping-pong (bounces back from the end, playing each end frame once) (initially Forward).
⑤ Loop When off, the preview plays the tag once and stops (initially on).
⑥ Color The tag strip color. Click the swatch or type a HEX value (initially blue, orange, green, red, purple, teal, yellow and gray in turn).
Editing and playing tags
Right-click menu of the idle tag
⑦ Tag box · ⑧ Tag right-click menu (Tag properties…, Play this tag, Delete)

Clicking a tag selects it (white outline), and the preview plays that tag in its direction (a tag with Loop off plays once and stops). Clicking the frame area outside tags (headers, cels, effect rows or empty space on the tag strip) deselects it, and the preview loops all frames again.
Tag names are used for By tag cell names and per-tag files in Export, and for the range in GIF export. Tags are saved in the .chickxel file.

Use layer effects when you want to add outlines, shadows, flashes or shakes without changing your drawing. To start, right-click a layer name in the timeline and choose Effects….
Effects only sit on top of the layer, so you can turn them off, change or delete them at any time, and they also apply to anything you draw later.
Basic workflow
Right-click menu of the Body layer name with Effects… (2), and the fx mark in the name cell
① Effects… · ② fx mark
In the timeline, right-click a layer name and choose ① Effects…. To cover only some frames, select those cels and choose Add effect… from the right-click menu.
On the Effects tab of the effects dialog, double-click an effect or drag it into the effect list in the middle.
Change values while watching the before/after preview, and drag in the frame strip below it to choose the frames the effect covers.
Click OK. The layer name gets ② fx, and each effect gets an effect row in the timeline.
To skip the dialog, drag an effect from the effect list panel onto a timeline cel (it goes in with default settings). Drag its range in the timeline effect row.
Order of effects
The same chick with an outline and a shadow applied in two different orders
Left: Outline → Shadow · Right: Shadow → Outline
Effects apply from the top of the list down, each on top of the result so far, so changing the order changes the result (see the picture).
Change the order with Up and Down in the effects dialog, or by dragging effect names in the timeline.
Clear an effect's checkbox to stop drawing it without deleting it.
Afterimage is always drawn last, wherever it is in the list.
To apply an effect only to what the effect above drew, turn on clipping (for example, rainbow colors on the outline only).
Layers with children
For a layer with child layers, pick the target in the common settings. This layer only applies to that layer's own drawing; Combined with children applies around the shape combined with its children (frame sheets only).
Applying permanently
Use Apply effect permanently when you want to turn an effect into real pixels and edit it like a drawing. Use the Apply permanently button in the effects dialog or the effect box's right-click menu; enabled effects above it become part of the drawing too.
Switch a Combined with children effect to This layer only before applying it permanently. Effects on locked layers can't be applied permanently.
Duplicating a layer also copies its effects, and Merge down turns the upper layer's effects into part of the drawing.
Where effects show
The canvas shows effects when Show effects on canvas is on; preview, frame sheets and layer atlases always include them.
While a layer with its own size is selected, the canvas shows that layer's and its parents' effects.
Timeline thumbnails show no effects (except cels with only a text effect and no drawing).
Layer atlases include only effects set to This layer only, and each sprite grows by the size of outlines or shadows.
Effects are drawn pixel by pixel, with no blur.
Effects this version doesn't know
Effects added in a newer Chickxel aren't drawn in this version, but saving doesn't remove them. The effect list shows them as a dimmed Unknown effect · type ID row that you can only reorder or delete.

Pressing Enter in a setting doesn't close the dialog. Changes apply only when you click OK, and everything you changed is a single undo step. Cancel or closing the window restores the original.

The effect list panel lets you drag effects onto timeline cels without opening the effects dialog. Click the ① Effects button (sparkle icon) on the toolbar to open ② the panel in the leftmost column.
Adding by drag and drop
While you drag a row over the timeline, ③ the target cel turns blue and the canvas and preview show the result right away. Inside a selected block of cels, the effect covers that block's frames.
Drop to add it with default settings (one undo step). Moving off the cels restores the preview.
Double-click a row to add it to the current layer at the current cel. The status bar shows where it went; drag its range in the effect row.
Finding effects
Like the effects dialog, it has Effects and Presets tabs, with a preview and name on each row (animated effects play).
Type in the Search effects box above the tabs to filter both tabs by name, description, author and store name.
Right-click a row and choose Add to favorites to move it to the Favorites group at the top of the tab; it stays there on the next launch. Remove from favorites undoes it.

With the file browser on too, the column splits into files (top) and effects (bottom). What you leave open is kept for the next launch.
Official effects
The effects you have from the start are the 23 official effects and Text. Official effects are script effects the app installs on first run, and they update automatically when the app contains a newer version. Bring back deleted official effects with Restore default effects in the Asset Manager.

pages.text:
Use these effects when you want to add an outline or shadow, or change an image's colors. They look the same on every frame.
Check the table below when choosing an effect or looking up what a setting does. Every color setting can be a solid color or a gradient (see Effect colors).
Effect What it does Main settings
Outline Draws a line around the image or on its inner edge. Shade from neighbors uses a darker version of the touching color instead of black. Color, Thickness, 8 directions (incl. corners), Inside (edge pixels), Hide original (outline only), Color mode, Shade %
Shadow Casts a shadow of the image's shape behind it, offset to the side. Color (semi-transparent black by default), X/Y offset, Dither
Edge light · shade Lights the edge facing the light and darkens the opposite edge for depth. Light direction, Range, Light color, Shade color
Color overlay Tints visible pixels with a color or gradient. At Amount 100% the image becomes a one-color silhouette. Color, Amount, Blend (Overlay / Multiply / Screen)
Inner glow Makes a glowing edge by blending a color inward from the edges. Color, Thickness, Strength, Weaker toward the inside, Blend (Screen by default)
Palette swap Swaps chosen colors for others (for example, red clothes → blue). Source → target (color pair list, up to 64 pairs), Tolerance 0–255
Color adjustment Turns the image grayscale or sepia, or adjusts hue, brightness, contrast or saturation. Style, Amount, Hue, Brightness/contrast, Saturation
Reflection Flips the image and reflects it below (water, floor), above or to the side (wall), fading out. Direction, Gap, Height %, Start and End opacity, Fade with dithering, Tint, Ripple
Text Writes text over the image. The Text tool (T) creates a new layer with this effect. Text (up to 1000 characters), Font, Bold/italic, Size, Color, Position, Box size (0 = auto), Scale, Letter and line spacing, Alignment, Smooth, Typewriter (one letter at a time)
Good to know
Dither: instead of semi-transparency, dots are spaced out so the area looks lighter. It gives a pixel-art look.
Text uses the bundled pixel fonts or fonts you added. Letters outside the image are cut off.
On an empty layer the Text effect works like a text layer; Merge down or applying it permanently turns it into pixels.

pages.text:
Use these effects for animated touches such as a hit, an explosion or a shake; they change from frame to frame. The more frames an effect covers, the slower it moves.
Pick an effect from the tables below, then tune its motion with the common Speed and Repeat settings (see common settings). Blink and Afterimage don't have these.
Flashing, appearing and changing colors
Effect What it does Main settings
Hit flash The image flashes one color, as if hit. Color, Strength, Count, Shape (Solid / Fade out)
Blink Repeatedly shows and hides (for example to show invincibility). Interval, Visible and Hidden frames, Count, Hide style (transparent / translucent / dots), Opacity
Appear / disappear The image gradually appears or disappears. Disappear (off = appear), Style (opacity / dots / wipe / pixel scatter), Wipe direction, Edge, Seed
Fade in · out The whole image gradually fades out or in. Fade out (off = fade in)
Light sweep A band of light sweeps across the image (the glint on coins or buttons). Angle, Width, Strength, Color, Softness
Color cycle Cycles through chosen colors so they flow like water, fire or neon. Colors (2–8), Steps, Reverse
Hologram Tints the image like a sci-fi hologram and adds scan lines, blinking and glitchy shifts. Color and strength, Scanlines, Bright band, Opacity, Dither, Blink, Glitch, RGB split, Edge glow, Seed
Moving
Effect What it does Main settings
Shake The whole image shakes. Direction (Horizontal / Vertical / Both), Strength, Count, Decay (weaker toward the end), Regular, Seed
Bob Floats gently up and down (or side to side) — floating items, idle motion. Height, Count, Direction
Squash & stretch Squashes and stretches like jelly, then returns to its shape. Horizontal and Vertical strength, Bounce, Anchor (feet fixed / center / pivot), Upward first
Rotate Rotates the image around an anchor, keeping pixel lines clean without adding new colors. Angle (360 = one turn, negative = counterclockwise), Pivot (feet fixed / center / pivot)
Afterimage Leaves faint copies of earlier frames behind for a sense of speed. Count, Spacing (frames), Opacity, Tint
Breaking apart and spreading
Effect What it does Main settings
Explode Pixels shatter and fly outward as they disappear. Fly distance, Center, Random variation, Gravity, Fragment size, Vanish, Flash, Keep original, Seed
Melt Pixels drip down, each column at its own speed. Distance, Irregularity, Drip (leaves trails), Vanish, Seed
Shockwave ring A pixel ring spreads out from the center. Center, Max radius, Thickness, Color, Fade out, Behind image
Good to know
Seed: a number that fixes a random look. Each click of the dice button gives another look, and the same seed always gives the same look.
Afterimage is drawn last, after all other effects.
When Shake or Bob moves the image, later effects' center point (pivot) can follow it (see Move pivot along).

pages.text:
See this page when you want an effect in gradient colors such as a rainbow, or want an effect to apply only to what the effect before it drew, such as color on the outline only.
Picking colors
Hit flash settings: color swatch, the Solid color/Gradient list opened, Clip to effect above
③ Color swatch · ④ Solid color / Gradient · ⑤ Clip to effect above
Clicking a ③ color swatch opens a color popup with the same modes as the main color editor, the palette, recent colors and buttons to pick from the image or screen; the canvas updates as you pick (see Color pickers in other windows).
Each color setting can be a ④ solid color / gradient. Gradient editing, color space and presets work as in the gradient tool.
Color popup opened from a color swatch: square picker, mode tabs, palette, and the Pick from image and Pick from screen buttons
Gradient modes
Choose the shape the gradient paints in. Static stays still; Animated flows or turns over the effect range.
Mode How it paints
Linear (static) · Linear (animated) Paints straight bands along the angle.
Radial (static) · Radial (animated) Paints rings spreading from the center.
Square (static) · Square (animated) Paints square bands spreading from the center (tilted by the angle).
Angular (static) · Angular (animated) Colors change going around the center (angle = starting point).
Whole sprite, one color (over time) The whole image is one color per frame and changes color over the effect range.
Depending on the shape, set the Direction, angle and Repeats/rotations (1–16).
Even an effect that doesn't move, such as Outline, changes color with an animated gradient.
Whole sprite, one color (over time) also has speed and ping-pong settings.
Clipping
Two chicks with a rainbow gradient Color overlay under an Outline: clipping off and on
Left: clipping off · Right: clipping on (Outline → gradient Color overlay)
Turn on ⑤ Apply to → Clip to effect above and the effect applies only to what the effect just before it drew. Above, the color overlay with clipping off covers the whole image (left); with it on, only the outline is colored (right).
Two chicks with a Shadow under an Outline: with clipping off the whole image casts a shadow behind it, with clipping on an outline-shaped shadow lies over the picture
Left: clipping off · Right: clipping on (Outline → Shadow)
A clipped effect can still spread beyond those pixels. A clipped shadow becomes a shadow of the outline alone, drawn over the picture (right).
Several clipped effects in a row build on each other (for example, Outline → Shadow → Color overlay colors the outline and its shadow together).
If the effect before is off or not on that frame, the clipped effect isn't shown either.
You can't clip to Afterimage, and clipping needs an effect before it.
Clipped to an outline with Hide original (outline only) on, an effect applies to the line only.

pages.text:
See this page when you want to set which frames an effect covers, how fast it moves and what remains after it ends. These are the common rows at the bottom of the effect settings.
Row Shown for What it sets
Apply to All effects Whether to apply only to what the effect before drew (clipping)
Speed · Repeat Animated effects (except Blink and Afterimage) How the motion speeds up and slows down and repeats
Later effects: Move pivot along Effects that move the image (Shake, Bob and so on) Whether later effects' center point (pivot) moves too
Cels after the range: Keep the end look Animated effects (when the range isn't All frames) Whether the final look stays after the range ends
The effect group in the tool options dock shows some of these rows too (range and clipping only in the effects dialog).
Effect range
The effect range is the frames an effect covers: All frames (including frames added later) or a start–end range.
Pick the range for new effects with Add range in the effects dialog.
Change an added effect's range by dragging in the dialog's frame strip or its timeline effect box.
Inserting or deleting frames grows or shrinks the range like a tag, and deleting all its frames deletes the effect.
Speed and repeat
Two rows of the same Shockwave ring over a 6-frame range: Linear on top, Fast start below
Top: Linear · Bottom: Fast start — frames 1–6 of the range from left
Speed: Fast start / Linear / Slow start / Slow start and end. Fast start moves a lot at first and almost stops at the end (see the picture).
Repeat: Once / Loop (start over) / Ping-pong (go and come back), 1–8 times.
Defaults differ by effect (for example, Explode and Shockwave ring use Fast start).
Later effects, Cels after the range and Expand canvas
Effects dialog showing pivot motion, keep the end look and the Expand canvas button in the common settings
① Move pivot along · ② Keep the end look after the range · ③ Expand canvas… button
For an effect that moves the image, choose ① whether later effects' center point (pivot) moves with it; for an animated effect, choose ② whether its final look stays after it ends (see below).
③ If an effect gets cut off at the canvas edge, use this button to grow the canvas (see Expanding the canvas).
Move pivot along
Effects dialog with Shake before Rotate and Move pivot along checked, with its displacement tooltip visible
⑤ Move pivot along and its tooltip
With Rotate after Shake, ⑤ Move pivot along (on by default) makes the rotation center follow the shaking image. Turn it off to shake only the image and keep the rotation center in place.
The row appears only for effects that report movement: the official Shake and Bob (1.0.2 or later) and script effects with ctx.movePivot in the source that are allowed to run.
The moved center is used by later effects that work around a center point, such as Rotate and Squash & stretch.
With a layer that has its own size selected, the pivot marker follows the moved position, and the original spot is shown as a small circle and dotted line.
Keep the end look
Timeline effect row showing a faint tail beyond the range and an even fainter tail over unlinked cels
⑥ Faint tail after the effect's range
Turn on Cels after the range: Keep the end look when you want an animated effect's final look to stay after it ends. For example, a throw over frames 1–18 stays landed on frame 19. The timeline shows ⑥ a faint tail.
Cels after the range that are linked to its last cel look exactly like it.
Unlinked cels keep only the moved position, and their tail is fainter.
With Move pivot along on, later effects' centers and the pivot marker follow the final position too.
It's unavailable when the range is All frames.
Unlinking such a cel puts the held look into its drawing.
Effect padding
Effects that draw outside the image, such as Outline, Shadow and Explode, reserve extra space (padding) around it. When exported to a layer atlas, each sprite grows by this padding. Effects that move the image widen it automatically by the distance moved.

Select cels and choose ⑱ Add effect… from the right-click menu to open the effects dialog with Add range set to those frames.
You can also drag a row from the effect list panel onto a timeline cel to add it with default settings.
Changing by dragging
Drag either end of a box to change its range, or drag the body to move the whole range. Double-click a box to open the effects dialog.
Drag an effect name up or down to reorder it, or drop it on another layer's row to move it to that layer. Select and press Delete to delete, Ctrl+C/V to copy.

Use script effects to add looks such as outlines, glows or shakes to a layer. They are layer effects written in JavaScript, added and edited in the effects dialog.
Official, Store and your own effects are all script effects. An effect's code (its source) is saved in the project file, so it draws the same on any computer.
In the effects dialog
Effects dialog with a script effect selected: my script effect tile at the end of the Effects tab, and the name, status line, edit buttons, Save as asset and settings in the settings panel

Received and own script effect tiles have a code icon at the top right. The tooltip shows the description and the Store name (or the author), and says so when the script isn't allowed to run.

Allowing scripts to run
Run script effects window: checkbox, name, author and hash for each script, Run and Don't run buttons

Opening a project with scripts you haven't seen before shows the Run script effects? window. ⑰ Each script has a checkbox, name, author and hash; ⑱ Run runs only the checked ones and Don't run runs none.
Your choice is remembered on this computer for each effect. Effects that don't run aren't drawn but stay in the project; allow them later with Allow to run in the settings.
These run without asking: sources written or imported on this computer, your own script effects, effects installed with the Asset Manager, sources written by the AI and official effects (older versions too).
Sources set to Don't run stay blocked until you allow or reinstall them.
When a script can't draw
A script effect that can't draw gets a warning icon at the end of its effect list row and on its timeline effect row. Hover the icon in the effect list for the reason.
Status Cause and fix
Missing source The project lacks the source. Open the same JS file with Open JS file… in the settings.
Not allowed The script isn't allowed to run. Click Allow to run in the settings.
Source error The code has syntax errors. Fix them in the editor.
Failed A frame went over the limits or an error occurred while running. Only this effect is skipped on that frame.
Stopped It failed 3 times in a row and stopped. Fix it, then click Run again in the settings or turn the effect off and on.
Good to know
Scripts run in an isolated engine with no file or network access, within time and memory limits per frame.

pages.text:
Reference for writing script effect code yourself or fixing code the AI wrote. This page covers the basic shape of the code and the items you put in effect({ … }) (declaration keys).
Shape of a source
One code file is one effect. Call effect({ … }) exactly once at the top; besides it, keep only const values and functions (no import or export).
render(img, ctx, s) is called for every frame. It changes the pixel values in img.data directly and returns nothing.
The same image, frame and settings must always give the same result. Date, Math.random, eval, Function, files, network, timers and console aren't available; use ctx.hash and ctx.random for randomness.
This is the skeleton New script starts from (comments removed). It has one Strength setting and moves the red of each non-transparent pixel toward 255 by that strength.
effect({
  name: "New effect",
  language: "en",
  settings: [
    { key: "strength", label: "Strength", type: "int", min: 0, max: 100, default: 50 },
  ],
  render(img, ctx, s) {
    const d = img.data, k = s.strength / 100;
    for (let i = 0; i < d.length; i += 4) {
      if (d[i + 3] === 0) continue;
      d[i] = lerp(d[i], 255, k);
    }
  },
});
Declaration keys
Use this table to set the effect's name, description and how it animates. All of these go inside effect({ … }).
Name Meaning
name Effect name (1–100 characters, required)
description Short description (up to 200 characters); the initial short description when publishing
author Author name (shown in the run confirmation window)
language Language of the name, description and setting labels ("ko", "en", "zh-Hans" …)
translations Other languages as { name, description, labels }; labels translate setting labels, choice labels and group titles
tags Up to 8 tags of lowercase English letters, digits and hyphens; used as tags when publishing
settings List of settings (see setting types)
gradients Initial gradients of color settings (optional). See Writing gradients below
render(img, ctx, s) Called for every frame; changes img.data in place
animated · motion · easing animated: true = changes over time (adds speed and repeat settings) · motion: false = hides speed and repeat · easing = initial easing ("Linear", "EaseIn", "EaseOut", "EaseInOut")
repeat · repeatCount · movePivot Initial values for animated effects: repeat mode Once, Loop or PingPong (default Once) · repeat count 1–8 (default 1) · whether later effects' centers move along (default true)
padding Margin for drawing outside the image: [left, top, right, bottom] or padding(s, width, height) { … } (see Drawing outside the image below)
area · radius "global" (default) = once per frame with the whole image · "local" = per tile, with radius px around it
deferred true = draws after all other effects regardless of its place in the list (like Afterimage). Only then ctx.renderedFrameSource is available
Writing gradients
Write one per color slot: a color setting "key", a list item "key[0]", or a pair side "key[0].from" or "key[0].to".
The value is { stops: [{ position, color }, …] }. position is 0–1 and color "#RRGGBB"; only stops is required.
Optional keys: alphaStops ({ position, alpha: 0–255 }), interpolation (Smooth, Steps), colorSpace (OkLch, OkLab, Rgb, Hsl), dither, shape (Linear, Radial, Square, Angular, Uniform), angle, reverse, cycles, animated, easing, pingPong. Left out, they take initial values.
When the effect is added, that color setting starts with this gradient; the user can change it or switch back to a solid color. A wrong slot or value is a declaration error.
The Effect Maker's Set as default writes the chosen gradients here for you.
Preview keys
Use this table to choose the chick and motion for previews in the Effect Maker. These apply only to the preview, Check and the published preview, never to documents.
Name Meaning
previewChick · previewEndChick Preview chick name (default "original") and end chick name. "none" = an empty canvas without a chick (for effects that draw on their own, such as rain or snow)
previewFrames Number of frames in the preview, the check and the published preview (2–20, default 10)
previewMotion Chick movement: "none" (default), "right", "left", "up", "down" (1 px per frame) or one [x, y] per frame (−32 to 32; later frames keep the last one)
previewPivot · previewEndOffset · previewEndPivot Offsets of each frame's pivot · the end chick's position · the last frame's pivot. Each is [x, y] px (−64 to 64, default 0; see preview position and pivot)
Chick names 1–10: original, painter, pencil, palette, easel, paint-bucket, designer, heart-canvas, cursor, hatch
11–20: knight, wizard, archer, ninja, pirate, astronaut, viking, king, gamer, healer
Drawing outside the image (padding)
img is the source image plus the declared margin (padding). Anything drawn outside it is cut off.
Effects that draw outside the source, such as glows, shadows, outlines, shakes, smoke, particles and ripples, must declare padding.
When the reach depends on the settings, compute it with padding(s, width, height) { return [left, top, right, bottom]; }. Otherwise give a fixed value of just the distance it reaches.
With padding the source starts at (ctx.source.x, ctx.source.y) inside img. Measure source-relative positions from ctx.source, ctx.center or ctx.pivot.

Keys of an item: key (id) · label (shown name) · type · min, max, step (range) · default (initial value) · choices · alpha (allow transparency) · widget (field style) · pair (paired setting) · group · when (show condition).
Fields and values by type
The field each type creates in the effects dialog, and the value render reads.
type Field in the effects dialog s.key value

bool Checkbox true / false

pages.text:
Reference for when render needs the image size, progress, colors, other layers and so on. img is the image to draw on; ctx holds run info and helpers.
Image (img)
Use these to read and write pixels.
Name Meaning
img.width · img.height · img.data Width and height of the padded image and its pixel array: four numbers R, G, B, A per pixel; the red of (x, y) is at (y * img.width + x) * 4. Written values are rounded to 0–255
img.blank(w, h) · img.blendOver(src, x, y) Makes an empty (transparent) image of the same kind · draws src over the image at (x, y), respecting transparency
Frame and position
Use these to change things over time or measure from a reference point.
Name Meaning
ctx.progress · ctx.phase · ctx.t How far the effect range has progressed (0–1). progress includes loop and easing (usually the one to use), phase only the loop, t neither
ctx.frame · ctx.step · ctx.span Frame being drawn (from 0) · frames since the first frame of the range · range length − 1
ctx.rangeStart · ctx.rangeEnd · ctx.frameTag First and last frame of the effect range (0 and the last frame in previews) · name of the tag containing this frame ("" when none or in previews)
ctx.source · ctx.pivot · ctx.center Where the source sits { x, y, w, h } · pivot (the effect's center point) { x, y } · source center { x, y } (always the middle, unlike the pivot)
ctx.movePivot(dx, dy) Reports how far the image moved (px, fractions allowed). Calls add up; returns nothing
ctx.position(key) Image coordinates { x, y } of a position setting. Custom = the source's top left + (X, Y), Canvas center = ctx.center, Pivot = ctx.pivot, Image center = middle of the picture before the effect
ctx.slice 9-slice border (the edge margins that stay fixed when stretched) { left, top, right, bottom } of the project or that layer. null when there is none or it doesn't fit
Colors and randomness
Use these to apply the user's colors or make random patterns.
Name Meaning
ctx.color(key, x, y, bounds?) · ctx.colorAt(key, i, x, y, bounds?) · ctx.pairColor(key, i, "from"|"to", x, y, bounds?) Color { r, g, b, a } of a color setting at (x, y). The solid color, or for gradients picked across the opaque area of the image (or the given bounds { x, y, w, h })
ctx.hasGradient(…) Whether a color slot has a gradient: "key", "key[0]", "key[0].from", or (listKey, index, "from"|"to")
ctx.gradientAt("slot", t, x?, y?) Color at t (0–1) of a gradient, for picking a color by a value (a particle's age, progress) instead of position. Ignores the gradient's shape and angle. x, y place the dot pattern (dither; default 0)
ctx.hash(x, y, seed, salt?) · ctx.random(seed) A fixed random number from 0 up to 1. hash depends on position, seed and a purpose number (salt); random on frame and seed. Always the same
ctx.bayer2(x, y) · ctx.bayer4(x, y) 2×2 (0–3) and 4×4 (0–15) dot-pattern thresholds (for mixing colors by dithering)
Other frames and layers
Use these when you need pictures from other frames or layers.
Name Meaning
ctx.frameSource(i) The source of frame i before effects (same size). null when missing or a different size
ctx.renderedFrameSource(i) Deferred effects only: frame i with this layer's other effects applied, { image, offsetX, offsetY }
ctx.matchPixels(a, b, mode?) Pairs the opaque pixels of two images (for transform effects). { count, data }, [ax, ay, bx, by] per pair. Mode "color" pairs by brightness (default: by position). null when a or b is null
ctx.layer(key) · ctx.layerWithEffects(key) · ctx.layerEffects(key) The layer chosen in a layer setting on this frame (without / with its effects, aligned to img) and its enabled effect names. null or an empty array when there is none
Text and global helpers
Use these to draw text or do number and color math.
Name Meaning
ctx.text(text, options?) Draws text into a transparent image with the Text effect's fonts and layout. options: font, size, color, bold, italic, smooth, align, letterSpacing, lineSpacing, width
lerp · hsvToRgb · rgbToHsv · rgbToOklab · oklabToRgb · Math lerp(a, b, t) = the value a fraction t between a and b · HSV and OKLab color conversion · Math (no Math.random). Typed arrays: Float64Array, Int32Array, Uint8Array
One floating damage number
This draws the text from a text setting with ctx.text, places it with img.blendOver and moves it up as the effect progresses.
effect({
  name: "Damage number",
  animated: true,
  settings: [
    { key: "message", label: "Shown text", type: "text", default: "42", max: 32 },
  ],
  render(img, ctx, s) {
    const label = ctx.text(s.message, { size: 12, color: "#ff6666", bold: true });
    const x = Math.floor((img.width - label.width) / 2);
    const y = Math.floor(img.height / 2 - ctx.progress * 12);
    img.blendOver(label, x, y);
  },
});

pages.text:
See this page when an effect is slow, looks cut off, or needs to read other layers or frames. It collects how to run fast and common patterns.
Fast path and limits
When render uses only numbers, booleans, loops, if, Math, lerp, helper functions taking numbers and img.data, it runs quickly on the fast path.
Strings, objects, arrays, closures, recursion and the like run on the general engine (Jint) with the same result, only slower.
These run on the fast path too: ctx.center, ctx.frameSource, ctx.matchPixels, ctx.position, ctx.movePivot, color functions (ctx.color and the like) with the key written literally, ctx.layer and ctx.layerWithEffects.
These run on Jint: ctx.slice, ctx.layerEffects, and reading layer or font setting values. The Effect Maker's status button shows which path is used and why.
Limits per frame: 2 seconds, 50 million statements, 256 MB of memory and call depth 256. Bigger images get 100 µs, 500 statements and 6 KB more per pixel.
Over a limit the frame is skipped; after 3 in a row the effect stops.
Keep the work proportional to the pixel count (no big loop per pixel).
Effects that move the image
Effects that move their image report the distance moved this frame (px) with ctx.movePivot(dx, dy). Later effects' centers, the layer pivot marker, the margin and held positions after the range then follow.
Effects that don't report it, such as Follow path or Gravity throw, need this call where the movement is computed (in Edit script) for others to follow.
Reading other layers
Add a layer setting so the user picks the layer, then read it in render with ctx.layer("key") (without effects), ctx.layerWithEffects("key") (with effects) or ctx.layerEffects("key") (enabled effect names). A layer can't be read by position or by a name in the code.
You get the nearest layer with the chosen name (excluding this layer and its parents; hidden layers count), aligned to img. Layer opacity isn't applied.
It is null when the layer is missing, so always check.
ctx.layerWithEffects skips that layer's effects that read other layers with effects, so layers reading each other never loop.
Changing the pixels, effects, name or order of the layer being read, or the 9-slice border, redraws right away. In the Effect Maker you preview it on a preview scene; publishing adds the layer-reference tag.
Effects that use several frames (transform)
ctx.frameSource(i) reads another frame before effects. Effects using it also draw on frames without a cel, so put pictures only on the first and last frames and apply the effect over that range to fill the frames between.
Preview and check it with the Effect Maker's end chick; publishing adds the frame-reference tag. ctx.frameTag lets an effect draw differently per frame tag.
How a transform effect works:
Read the first and last pictures with a = ctx.frameSource(ctx.rangeStart) and b = ctx.frameSource(ctx.rangeEnd).
Pair the pixels of the two pictures with m = ctx.matchPixels(a, b).
Clear img.data, then draw each pair moved from (ax, ay) toward (bx, by), blending position and color by ctx.progress.
Randomness
Random looks come from a seed. Add a { key: "seed", type: "int", … } setting to get a dice button in the effects dialog.
ctx.hash(x, y, s.seed, salt) and ctx.random(s.seed) always give the same value for the same seed.
Give each random value its own salt (a purpose number, e.g. 0 = direction, 1 = speed).
Feed values that don't change per frame, such as a piece number, so each piece follows the same path in every frame.
Following gradient colors
Users can switch color settings to gradients. Pick the color for each pixel you write with ctx.color("key", x, y) (lists ctx.colorAt, pairs ctx.pairColor) so gradients are followed.
Use s.key only when one color is really needed.
Pass bounds { x, y, w, h } as the last argument when the default area doesn't fit the shape. To pick a color by a value such as a particle's age or progress, use ctx.gradientAt("key", t, x, y).
The declaration's gradients can make a color setting start as a gradient. The Effect Maker's Check points out color settings that draw in one color only.

pages.text:
Use the Effect Maker when you want to make a new script effect or change one of yours. Open it with AI > Effect Maker…, preview it on sample chicks, then publish it to the Store if you like.
You can also open it with the Effect Maker button at the bottom of the effect list or Edit in Effect Maker on your script effect. Opened without an effect, it starts on a new script with the AI panel open.
The title, description, tags and preview chick are written into the effect's code too, so one code file is one effect. Effect presets (bundles of effects) aren't made here.
Basic workflow
Start from the skeleton with New script, or pick one of your effects in the list.
Edit the source yourself, ask in the AI panel, or copy the Rules window to another AI and paste its answer.
Check the look in the preview. Edits are saved automatically, so the effect is ready on the Effects tab of the effects dialog.
To share it, run Check on the 20 sample chicks and click Upload….
Window layout
Effect Maker window: my effects list and info on the left, code editor and preview setting values in the middle, chick preview and frame strip on the right, Undo, Insert, status, Check and Upload buttons at the bottom
① My effects list · ② New script and Open JS file · ③ Info · ④ Rules · ⑤ Code editor · ⑥ Preview setting values · ⑦ AI · ⑧ Preview and frame strip · ⑨ Preview chick and end chick · ⑩ Play, show without effect, frames, motion, position and pivot · ⑪ Undo and Insert into layer · ⑫ Status button · ⑬ Check, Upload, Close
① My effects: effects made on this computer or published with your account. Turn on Show all at the top right to also see received effects and unchanged copies of them (see My effects list).
② New script starts from a short skeleton; Open JS file… opens a .js file as a new effect.
③ Info: title, description, tags and Languages (see Info and languages).
④ Rules (right of the Info header, book icon): shows the rules for writing effects (see Rules window).
⑤ The code editor is the same as the script editor of the effects dialog (see Script editor). Ctrl+Z undoes.
⑥ Preview setting values: pick the setting values used for the preview (see below).
⑦ AI (right of the Preview header, sparkles icon) opens and closes the AI panel on the right.
⑧ The preview is the same image that is made when you publish (0.1 s per frame). Click a frame in the strip to pause on it.
⑨ Preview chick: pick one of 20 chicks, or None in the first slot (an empty canvas, for effects that draw on their own such as rain or snow). End chick (transform effects) is covered separately.
⑩ Play/pause icon button, Show without effect, Frames (2–20), and the motion (gear) and position (crosshair) buttons (see Moving the preview chick).
⑪ The red Undo steps back through source edits one at a time; Insert into layer adds the effect to the current layer in the main window (see below).
⑫ The status button shows the current state by color; click it for details (see Status, check and publishing).
⑬ Check, Upload… and Close.
Preview setting values
They appear in the same order as in the right dock: the effect's settings, then easing, repeat and repeat count for animated effects, then 'move later effects' center along' for effects that move the image.
'Cels after the range: Keep the end look' is fixed off.
Reset goes back to the effect's defaults.
Set as default saves the current values and chosen gradients as the effect's defaults.
Easing, repeat and pivot motion left at the app defaults (Linear, Once, 1, true) aren't written into the code.
Saving, undo and inserting
There is no Save button. An edit is saved as your script effect once you stop editing for 1.5 seconds (with the preview scene).
Ctrl+S saves right away.
While the code has errors it isn't saved, and the window title ends with *. Choosing another effect or closing then asks Save, Discard or Cancel.
A new script is saved once your first edit has no errors.
Undo uses the same history as Ctrl+Z, up to 300 steps. It undoes title, description, tag and default edits too, but not preview scene edits.
Insert into layer adds the effect with the preview setting values to the end of the current layer's effects (all frames, one undo step). If the effects dialog is open or the layer is locked, you only get a message.

pages.text:
Use the Info area on the left of the Effect Maker to set the effect's name, description and tags or add names in other languages. Editing it updates the code too.
Title, description and tags
The header shows the developer on the right: the author's profile picture and name for Store effects, a person icon and 'Made on this computer' for effects made on this computer.
Fill in Title (1–100 characters), Description (up to 200) and Tags. They are name, description and tags in the code.
Type tags like #neon and press Space, Enter or a comma to add a chip. Remove one with X or Backspace in the empty field; up to 8, lowercase English letters, digits and hyphens.
The language you are editing shows next to the field names. When the UI language differs from the effect's base language, you edit that language's translation (dim text is the base value).
Effects without a base language (language) show the UI-language translation if there is one, else the written values (Base (language not set)).
Languages
Languages opens a window for the title, description and setting labels in each language. The name for the app's UI language shows in the effects dialog, the layer effect list and the Asset Manager.
Add or remove languages, or type another language code. Empty fields show the base-language value; languages with text are green with a check mark.
Setting group titles can be translated too.
Base language at the top is the language the title and description were written in. OK writes it into the code as language.
Without a base language it is guessed from the letters: Hangul → Korean, kana → Japanese, Han → Simplified Chinese, Cyrillic → Russian, Thai → Thai, Latin → English.

What the AI does
It adds useful settings on its own and lists them briefly in its answer. It reads other layers through a layer setting and picks colors per pixel so gradients are followed.
It can look at the open drawing, layers, effects and references but can't change them. It can also read your other script effects ("like my X effect, but …").
Saving, inserting into the layer and publishing are up to you with the buttons below.
Ask and it searches and reads the web (it doesn't otherwise). It can't see a page's pictures or animation, so it works from the descriptions and rewrites any code it saw with the app's effect API.
Message queue
Pressing Enter or Send while the AI's turn is running puts the message in the queue above the input; queued messages are sent in order when the turn ends (even when stopped).
Each row has a drag handle (change the order), edit (pencil), delete (trash can) and Send now.
Edit brings the message back into the input; Send now stops the running turn and sends it right away.

Installing
Pick an asset in the list (⑦). Narrow it down with the filter, search or tags.
Clicking Install shows a progress bar and Cancel in its place.

Updates tab
Check for updates downloads the online list again and shows, for each asset with a new version, an 'Installed 1.0.0 → new version 1.1.0' row and an Update to … button.
New versions are installed only when you click. The tab name shows the number of updates (e.g. Updates (1)), or 'All received assets are up to date.' when there are none.

Store versions and local edits
Assets from the Store stay linked to their package and are overwritten only by a higher version. Local edits are replaced without asking; favorites stay.
To keep your changes, first make a copy with Copy to My Assets; updates never overwrite the copy. Received script effects are read-only in the Effect Maker too.
Effects already placed in a project don't change when the asset is updated or deleted.
If the downloaded file doesn't match the online list, Chickxel reports an error and changes nothing.

pages.text:
Use this to give effects, gradients and shape pen sets to a friend or to receive theirs. Assets travel in .chickxel-asset files, several per file.
Exporting
On the Installed tab, filter by kind and search by name until only the assets to send are shown.
Click Export… and choose where to save. All assets shown go into one file.
Send the file to the other person.
Each asset in the file keeps its author. Assets you made get your signed-in account's name as author.
If you send a single Store asset unchanged, the other person also gets its Store updates.
Asset details have no export button; only your own shape pen sets export one at a time with the Export menu in their details (see Managing shape pen sets).
Importing
Click Import from File… and pick a .chickxel-asset file, or double-click the file.
Chickxel checks the file first. If anything is wrong, each problem is listed and nothing is added.
If it passes, the assets inside are added one by one.
An asset that needs a newer Chickxel tells you which version.
If Chickxel is already running, a double-clicked file opens in that window. On Windows, it works after you have started Chickxel once (see Installation).
Overlapping assets
If the same asset already exists, choose Replace, Keep Both or Skip in the Import Asset window. Turn on Apply to the remaining items to do the same for the remaining overlaps.
Importing a file asks for every overlap. Downloading from the Store asks only when an asset with the same content isn't linked to the Store.

pages.text:
Publishes one of your assets to the Store and chickxel.com with your Chickxel account. Open it with Publish Online… at the top of the Installed tab or in your asset's details.
Publish Online window: Author (profile picture, display name and @handle), Package (mode line, name, short description, languages, package ID, version, tag chips) and License CC0-1.0 on the left; the asset to publish, list preview, pre-upload checks and the Upload button on the right
⑨ Author · ⑩ Package · ⑪ License · ⑫ Asset to publish · ⑬ List preview · ⑭ Pre-upload check
⑨ Author: the profile picture, display name and @handle of your signed-in account. Change them in Help > Chickxel Account…, not here (the handle is fixed once you upload a package).
⑩ Package: the top line says whether this is a new package or an update of one of yours. The fields are in the Package fields table below.
⑪ License: always CC0-1.0. Anyone may use the asset without conditions (even commercially, without credit); the package includes the text as LICENSE.txt.
⑫ Asset: the name and kind of the asset being published.
⑬ List preview: the picture shown in the Store and on chickxel.com. It starts as an automatic preview made from the asset; Replace with Image File… uses a PNG (up to 512×512, 1 MB) and Use Asset Preview goes back. The automatic preview also includes the original without the effect, compared by hovering on chickxel.com.
⑭ Pre-upload check: checked as you type, with the server's rules. A red X is an error (blocks uploading); an orange exclamation mark is a warning (you can still upload).
Package fields
Field What it does
Name, short description The name and a description of up to 200 characters shown in the Store. Script effects fill these in from their declaration.
Languages… Adds a name and short description per language, shown to people viewing in that language. Languages with text show in green.
Package ID Set automatically and can't be edited: the ID of your published package if the asset came from it, otherwise 'handle.name'. Rename to publish a different package.
Version Suggests the next patch version (1.0.0 → 1.0.1). It must be higher than any version already published.
Tags Type tags like #neon and add them with Space, Enter or a comma; remove one with its X or Backspace in an empty field. Up to 8, lowercase English letters, digits and hyphens, 32 characters each.
Uploading
With no errors, a blue check says all checks passed and Upload turns on. Click it.
While uploading, the button shows 'Uploading… N%' with a progress bar, then 'Checking on server…' after the transfer. Cancel Upload stops it.
Once uploaded, the package appears right away in the Store and on chickxel.com (chickxel.com/packages/<ID>). Click Open website in the message to open its page. Later uploads become new versions of the same package.
Checks and tags
Main errors: wrong package ID, version, name, description, language settings or tag format; no list preview; a name that clashes with another package; a version not higher than one already published. Warning: no tags.
Effects that read other layers get the layer-reference tag, effects that read other frames frame-reference, and effects using ctx.movePivot pivot-move, automatically. These tags can't be removed and count toward the 8; if there's no room, an error asks you to remove another tag.
If the server rejects the package, the reason appears at the end of the checks as 'Rejected by the server: …'.
Good to know
If you aren't signed in, the account window opens first.
One asset makes one package. To publish a received asset, copy it to My assets and publish the copy. Effect presets can't be published; publish effects as script effects.
When the app language differs from the package's base language, the name and description fields edit the app-language translation. Edit the base-language text at the top of the Languages… window.
A package deleted on chickxel.com disappears from the site, the Store and your profile, and its XP and storage quota are returned. Until an admin restores or permanently deletes it, its ID can't be used again.

Read this when you start drawing. The mouse buttons, keys and where paint goes work the same in every drawing tool.
Mouse buttons
Button What it does
Left button Paints with the ① primary color.
Right button Paints with the ② secondary color.
The other button while drawing Cancels that stroke. The status bar shows Cancel stroke.
With ③ Right button = eraser on, the right button of the pencil, gradient pencil, shape and fill tools erases.
Turn it on in the Options group of the tool options or in Drawing options in the Tools menu.
Tools where the buttons differ: Dodge/burn (lighten/darken), Dithering (swaps the two colors), the Eyedropper (which color gets the pick) and Gradient (left button only).
Using keys
④ The top bar always shows what the current tool can do.
Key What it does
Shift+click Draws a straight line from the end of the last stroke to where you click. Shapes keep their proportions; the gradient snaps to 45°.
Alt While held, the tool becomes the eyedropper.
Ctrl While held, the tool becomes the Move tool.
Ctrl+wheel Changes the brush size by 1.
[ / ] Decreases or increases the brush size by 1 (1–32).
X Swaps the primary and secondary colors.
Where paint goes
With a selection, you paint only inside it.
With symmetry drawing on, every tool except the gradient also paints at the mirrored spots (Brush settings).
In tile mode, strokes that cross an edge continue on the opposite side.
If the layer is locked, nothing is drawn and the status bar shows The current layer is locked and can't be drawn on..
Drawing commands in the Edit menu
The Edit menu opened
⑤ Add outline · ⑥ Replace color · ⑦ Clean up lines · ⑧ Flip/rotate · ⑨ Canvas size
Edit menu commands change the whole picture or the selection at once. Each is one undo step.
Command What it does
⑤ Add outline (primary color) (Ctrl+Alt+O) Add outline (with diagonals) Adds a 1 px outline in the primary color around the drawing. Add outline (with diagonals) also fills diagonal pixels.
⑥ Replace color… (Ctrl+Alt+R) Changes every pixel of one color to another in the current layer and frame. The window's Color to replace and New color start as the primary and secondary colors. With a selection, Selection only limits it.
⑦ Clean up lines… Redraws outlines and inner lines as clean 1 px lines and arcs (Clean up lines).
⑧ Flip horizontal (selection/cel) (Shift+H) Flip vertical (selection/cel) (Shift+V) Flips the selected pixels, or the current layer's picture in this frame when nothing is selected.
⑧ Rotate 90° (selection/canvas) (Ctrl+R) Rotate -90° (selection/canvas) (Ctrl+Shift+R) Rotates the selected pixels by 90°; press Enter to drop them. With nothing selected, the whole canvas turns with all frames.
⑨ Canvas size… (Ctrl+Alt+C) Sets the new size and image position on the canvas (Canvas size mode).

pages.text:
Use this to draw or fix the same thing on several frames at once. A stroke on the current frame also lands at the same spot on the other frames in the range.
How to use it
Choose a Range in the Apply to frames group of the tool options (table below).
For ranges with frames before or after, enter the counts in Before and After (1–999). The affected frames show below, in orange when there is more than one.
Draw on the current frame. The same spot on the same layer's other frames gets it too.
Ranges
Range Frames that also get the stroke
Current frame only Only the current frame (default).
Up to N frames before The current frame and N frames before it.
Up to N frames after The current frame and N frames after it.
Before and after The current frame plus N before and M after.
Back to the first frame From the first frame to the current one.
On to the last frame From the current frame to the last one.
All frames Every frame.
How each tool applies
Check this table if you wonder what lands on the other frames.
Tool On the other frames
Pencil, eraser (100% strength), dither, shape, gradient pencil, curve pen Paints the same color on the same pixels.
Lighten/darken, eraser with partial strength Changes that frame's pixels by the same amount.
Shape Pen Stamps the same shapes over that frame.
Replace color brush Changes only pixels of the color first pressed on.
Fill Fills the same spot again based on that frame's drawing.
Gradient Paints again with the same start and end points.
Good to know
All frames together are one undo step. The status bar shows how many frames changed.
Linked cels are changed once. Locked layers and empty layers that arrange their children are skipped.
Empty cels get drawn on too. The canvas shows only the current frame.
The range resets to Current frame only each time the app starts. The counts are remembered.

Exporting and importing sets
Press Manage sets… to open the Asset Manager and select your set.
Choose Export > Set file (.chickxel-shapes)… in its details and save. You get one .chickxel-shapes file.
Give the file to someone or move it to another computer.

Getting and publishing sets in the Store
Get: install a set from the Shape pen filter on the Store tab of the Asset Manager. It gets updates too.
To change a received set, press Copy to my sets in its details. The original keeps getting updates.
Publish: press Publish Online… (or Publish New Version… once published) in your set's details to open the publish window. Sign-in is required.

New set from the canvas
New set from canvas… (film icon) in the Shape pen filter of the Asset Manager makes a new set from the current document. It asks for a name, adds the set at the end of yours and selects it.
Each frame becomes one shape, and empty frames are skipped. Use it to turn shapes drawn across one document's frames into a set at once.

With more than 64 shapes or a side over 256px, you are told which frames are the problem and nothing is written.
The canvas is the size of the largest shape; each shape is centered in its frame.
A received set is copied to your sets first and the copy opens. If you are its author, it is edited in place.
An already open set goes to its tab. This tab never asks about saving a project file.

Shape How to draw
Line From press to release. Shift = 15° steps
Curve Drag both ends, release, then move the mouse to bend. Same button or Enter confirms; the other button or Esc cancels. Shift = 15° steps, or an arc while bending
Rectangle The dragged box. Shift = square
Ellipse An ellipse in the dragged box. Shift = circle
Equilateral triangle The dragged line is one side (drag right to point up). Shift = 30° steps

pages.text:
The Eyedropper (I) picks a color from the canvas into the primary or secondary color. Use it to reuse a color already in the picture.
Picking colors
Left-click picks into the primary color, right-click into the secondary color. Drag to keep picking; the color where you release stays.
Source: All visible layers (default) picks the color you see; Current layer picks only from the current layer.
While a selection is being moved, its pixels are picked first.
Clicking outside the canvas picks from a normal layer's pixels outside the canvas.
Temporary eyedropper with Alt
Hold Alt in a drawing tool to use the eyedropper for a moment. Left-click sets the primary color, right-click the secondary; release to return.
Works in: Pencil, Gradient Pencil, Eraser, Fill, Gradient, Shape, Dodge/burn, Dithering and the Replace color brush.
It does not work in the text, selection, move, pivot and 9-slice tools.
It uses the eyedropper tool's Source setting.
An Alt used this way doesn't open the menu bar when released.

The Dithering tool paints the pixels under the brush in the primary and secondary colors following a pattern. Use it to mix two colors into an in-between tone with dots.
The left button paints the pattern pixels primary and the rest secondary. The right button swaps them.
The pattern is fixed to canvas coordinates, so overlapping strokes always line up.
The brush, symmetry, the selection and Shift+click lines work as with the pencil. There is no default shortcut.
Patterns

pages.text:
Use this when you want to move, copy, delete or flip only the part you selected. Without a selection, the same commands apply to the cel or the whole canvas.
Moving and deselecting
Action Result
Drag inside the selection (rectangle, ellipse, lasso), or drag with the Move tool Lifts the selected part and moves it. Until you drop it, it is a floating selection.
Ctrl+Shift+Left Ctrl+Shift+Right Up Down Moves it by 1px.
Shift+Left Shift+Right Shift+Up Shift+Down Moves it by 8px.
Enter Drops the floating selection where it is.
Right-click the canvas with a selection tool, Ctrl+D, Esc Drops it and removes the selection.
Ctrl+A Selects the whole canvas.
Plain arrow keys change frames. After you click the canvas with the Move tool, plain arrows move pixels too.
Select all (Ctrl+A) from another tool switches to rectangle select.
Pasting switches to rectangle select (unless rectangle, ellipse or lasso select is active).
Pixels on a locked layer can't be moved.
Commands that use the selection
Command With a selection Without a selection
Cut Ctrl+X Moves the pixels to the clipboard. Does nothing.
Copy Ctrl+C Copies the pixels. Copies the whole visible image of the current frame.
Paste Ctrl+V Pastes at the selection's top left. Pastes where it was copied.
Delete Delete Clears to transparent. Deletes the frames, layers or cels selected in the timeline.
Flip horizontal (selection/cel) Shift+H · Flip vertical (selection/cel) Shift+V Flips the selected part. Flips the current cel.
Rotate 90° (selection/canvas) Ctrl+R · Rotate -90° (selection/canvas) Ctrl+Shift+R Rotates the selected part by 90°. Rotates the whole canvas.
Transform (rotate/size)… Ctrl+T Opens the selection in transform mode. Opens the whole drawing of the current cel.
Add outline (primary color) Ctrl+Alt+O Adds a 1px outline around the drawing inside the selection. Adds it across the whole current cel.
Drawing tools (pencil, fill, shapes and so on) Paint only inside the selection. Paint anywhere.
Good to know
Pixels copied in the app paste at the same spot, even on another frame or layer.
A frame image copy pastes at (0,0), and images from other programs at the top left of the visible canvas.
On a layer with its own size, select all and copying without a selection cover only that layer's area.
Copying on the canvas clears cels or frames copied in the timeline, so pasting after clicking the timeline still pastes these pixels.
With a selection, delete clears only the selected part, even after you click the timeline.
With a selection, the Replace color… window offers Selection only.

pages.text:
The pivot is the point an image turns or flips around. Use the Pivot tool (K) when you want to set the rotation center or the Unity sprite's reference point.
Every layer has its own pivot, and exports use the canvas pivot.
Pivot tool on a 6-frame sample with the Body layer's pivot moved to the feet from frame 3 on: the pivot mark on the canvas, Tool options and pivot marks on the timeline cels
① Pivot mark on the canvas · ② 5×5 buttons · ③ X and Y · ④ From current frame on · ⑤ Target (top of the group) · ⑥ Cels with their own pivot (orange diamond at the cel's top left)
Moving the pivot
① Drag on the canvas and the pivot mark (a circle with a cross) follows; on release it is set, snapped to half pixels (one undo step).
② The 5×5 buttons jump to spots such as the edges, quarters and the middle. For odd sizes the middle rounds down (49 → 24).
③ X is measured in pixels from the left and Y from the bottom (as in Unity, in 0.5px steps).
To see the pivot with other tools, turn on View menu Show pivot (Pivot on the top bar).
Other layers' pivots then show as small labeled dots too (Canvas).
When an effect such as shake moves the image, the pivot mark moves with it; the original spot shows as a small circle and dotted line.
Target
⑤ The pivot you are changing is named at the top of the group. Normally it is the layer selected in the timeline. To change the canvas pivot, click the Canvas W×H text at the timeline's top left.
Kind Pivot that changes
Normal layer That layer's pivot
Layer with its own size That layer's pivot, measured from its own area (used by the layer atlas)
Empty layer that arranges children That layer's pivot. Set it only with the ② buttons and ③ numbers (dragging moves the children).
Canvas pivot The reference point for sheet and Unity exports
To match the canvas pivot to one layer's pivot, pick a Representative. It then follows that layer's pivot in every frame.
The representative layer gets a crown before its name in the timeline.
You can also set it from the layer's right-click menu.
From current frame on
④ Turn it on when the pivot must change partway, as in a walk cycle. The current frame through the last get their own pivot (and position, for a layer with its own size).
Changing the pivot then shifts this and later frames by the same amount. Earlier frames stay.
Turning it off removes the separate pivots and goes back to the default pivot.
⑥ Cels with their own pivot show an orange diamond at their top left.
To change just one frame, use the frame header's right-click menu (Use a separate pivot for this frame only / Reset pivot to default).
Applying a transform without a selection, or permanently applying an effect with Move pivot along on to a layer with its own size, also creates separate pivots.
Where pivots are used
Check this when you want to know what a pivot change affects.
Pivot Used for
Canvas pivot (or the representative layer's pivot) The sprite reference point in Unity exports and sheets
Layer pivot The starting rotation center of a transform and Transform whole layer, Around pivot in symmetry drawing, and that layer's layer effects (including scripts)
Canvas size mode and flipping or rotating the canvas move every pivot with the image.
Transform whole layer moves that layer's pivots.
A transform without a selection and a Move tool drag move that frame's pivot (not a right-drag).
Older .chickxel files without layer pivots open and look the same. Once saved, older versions can't open them.

rows.t: File types and where they go

pages.text:
This chapter covers opening files, keeping your work safe while you edit, and saving. Everything you edit lives in a single project file (.chickxel). For exporting outputs, see the Export and sharing chapter.
Task Pages
Open Opening files, Opening PNGs, Opening images, animations and videos, Dropping images onto the canvas, Importing 3D models
While you edit Autosave, Undo history that survives closing, Revert to saved
Save Saving, File types and where they go, Export cell names, Cleaning up old outputs
Close Save prompt when closing
Settings and problems Preferences, When errors occur
Read this to find out which files are made and where. You edit the project file (.chickxel); the other files are rebuilt from it when you save.
Files that are made
Unless you change the name or folder, everything is made next to the project and named after it. The example below is for saving hero.chickxel.
File Default name Made when
Project file hero.chickxel Every save. Layers, frames, effects and export settings are all stored here.
Frame sheet hero.png The sheet row is checked for saving (the default)
Layer atlas hero_parts.png There is a layer tree and the layer atlas is on
Unity settings files hero.png.meta, hero_parts.png.meta The game engine is Unity
Sprite Library One default plus one per skin preset Unity, with Sprite Library on
Unity prefab and animations hero.prefab, hero_idle.anim, hero.controller Unity, with Prefab or Animation on
Godot 4 hero.tres, hero.tscn The game engine is Godot 4
JSON hero.json The game engine is JSON
GIF, APNG and frame PNGs hero_idle.gif That row is checked for saving
Asset package .chickxel-asset You export assets in the Asset Manager. Double-click it to import.
Splitting per tag, skin or layer makes several files with that name added. Change names and folders in the Export dialog.
Hiding export paths
Export folders and names are saved so only this computer can read them (export path encryption), so sharing a .chickxel doesn't reveal your folders. On another computer, or after the settings folder is deleted, they go back to the defaults (the project folder and name).
Older and newer files
Files saved by this version can't be opened by older versions of Chickxel.
Older files are converted without asking and look the same. Groups become empty parent layers with the same name (Importing old files), and pivots carry over (Pivot tool).
A file from a newer Chickxel isn't opened; you're told so. Update the app.
Older projects from before the game engine choice open with Unity if they were writing Unity files, otherwise with None.
Good to know
Opening an exported PNG opens the project that made it (Opening PNGs).
Pixels pushed outside the canvas and script effects are saved in the project file too.
Effects this version doesn't know aren't drawn, but saving doesn't remove them. .gpixel files from the former name (Gpixel) open too.
Undo history, the app trash and preferences are in the settings folder, not in the project file.
