pages.text:
Read this when you want to open a project, picture or video to edit it. Each file opens in its own document tab; a file that is already open switches to its tab.
Ways to open
Method How
File menu File > Open (.chickxel · image · GIF · video)… (Ctrl+O). Pick several files to open a tab for each.
Recent files Pick from File > Recent files or the start screen (up to 10; Clear list empties it). Folders are in Recent folders.
File browser Click a file in the file browser on the left. Choose its folder with File > Open folder… or Open Unity project….
Dropping on the window Drop files outside the canvas (file list, start screen, tab strip, panels) to open them in new tabs. Images dropped on the canvas become layers.
Explorer · Finder Double-click a .chickxel file (see below).
What each file type opens as
File Opens as
.chickxel, .gpixel That project.
PNG The project that made the PNG, otherwise a new imported project (Opening (importing) PNGs).
JPG, BMP, GIF, WebP, ICO, animated PNG A new document with one frame per image frame (Opening images, animations and videos).
Videos (MP4, WebM, MOV, …), AVIF, HEIC Turned into frames in a new document (needs ffmpeg). Videos first show the Import video window.
3D models (GLB, glTF, OBJ, FBX) Set the angle, light and frames in the Import 3D model window; the drawn frames become a new document (Opening 3D models).
Opening by double-clicking in Explorer or Finder
Double-clicking a .chickxel opens it in Chickxel, and a .chickxel-asset imports the assets inside. File associations work like this on each OS.
OS File association
Windows Associated once you start the app (no administrator rights needed). If you move the exe, start it once again.
macOS Associated once Chickxel.app is in the Applications folder.
Linux None yet. Open files with File > Open or by dropping them.
If the app is already running, the file opens as a tab in that window.
If another app opens .chickxel files, right-click the file and choose Chickxel under Open with (Windows) or Open With (macOS).
Previews in Windows Explorer
In Explorer's Medium icons, Large icons and Extra large icons views, a .chickxel shows its first frame. An older file that shows the app icon gets its picture after one more save.
Files changed outside the app
When another program (a sync app, another Chickxel window, …) changes an open file, Chickxel does this.
Case What happens
The document you are viewing Asks whether to reload. With No the document stays as is, and saving afterwards overwrites the changed file.
Another tab without unsaved edits Reread when you switch to that tab.
Another tab with unsaved edits Keeps your edits and notes it in the status bar. Saving overwrites the changed file.

pages.text:
Opening a PNG opens the project that made it (such as a .chickxel with the same name in the same folder). Otherwise the PNG is imported as a new project.
Saving an imported PNG
An imported project saves to a .chickxel with the same name next to the PNG (hero.png → hero.chickxel). The first Ctrl+S saves there without asking.
Saving rewrites the original PNG as the project's output and keeps the guid of its existing .meta. There is no autosave until the first save.
Sheets with cell information
The Import PNG dialog, with As child layers marked 1 and As animation frames marked 2
① As child layers · ② As animation frames
If the .meta next to the PNG (Unity Multiple) has cells of different sizes, it's imported as child layers: one empty layer named after the file, with a child layer per cell (keeping name, size, pivot and border).
If there are two or more cells of the same size, you're asked to choose ① As child layers or ② As animation frames.
Importing as animation frames makes one frame per cell, and each cell's name becomes that frame's export cell name. Frames are aligned on each cell's pivot.
Splitting sheets without cell information
The Frame·Layer menu opened, with Split into frames by grid marked 3
③ Split into frames by grid in the Frame·Layer menu
The Split into frames by grid dialog with the method list open, marked 4
④ Split method: Grid - cell size / Grid - cell count / Auto (per blob)
The Split into frames by grid dialog, with the cell size, cell count and auto minimum size rows marked 5 to 7
⑤ Cell size (Cell width · Vertical) · ⑥ Cell count (Columns · Rows) · ⑦ Auto: minimum size
Use ③ Frame·Layer > Split into frames by grid: ④ pick the method and split by ⑤ cell size, ⑥ cell count or ⑦ automatically (by blobs).

Press Ctrl+S (① File > Save (+ export sheets)) to keep your work in a file. The export rows checked for saving are made too, and ② the status bar shows the result.
What a save does
The .chickxel is written (first to a temporary ….chickxel-tmp file, which then replaces the original).
Every export row checked for saving is made (files that are made). If none is checked, the status bar adds (export off).
Old outputs no longer made are moved to the app trash (Cleaning up old outputs).
The status bar shows the saved file and the exported sheets and cell counts, and the file is added to recent files and undo history.
The name on first save
The first save of a new project suggests its temporary title as the name (sprite if there is none). If the name is taken, a free name such as sprite_1 is used.
Save as
After Ctrl+Shift+S (File > Save as…), later saves go to the new file. The original file and its outputs stay, and outputs with the default name are made under the new name.
Exporting without saving
Export in the Export dialog writes only the selected row without saving the .chickxel. A never-saved document asks for a save location first.
If saving fails
The Save failed dialog, with the message that the project was saved but the sheet export failed marked 3
③ The project was saved but exporting the sheet/.meta failed (Save failed)
If the .chickxel was saved but only the outputs failed, ③ you're told so, and the project counts as saved.
Message Meaning and what to do
Couldn't save The .chickxel couldn't be written. Remove the cause and save again, or save under another name.
The file is read-only Turn off read-only in the file's properties, or save under another name.
Another program has the file open Close that program (image viewer, game engine, …) or save under another name.
Export file names collide The project is saved and only the export fails. Make the sheet, tag, layer or skin names, or the names and folders of list rows, differ.
When saving takes a while
If saving or opening takes a while, a progress box covers the whole window until it finishes; drawing, shortcuts and file drops are ignored meanwhile. Closing the window then closes it after the save.

Use this to turn your art into files for games or other programs, such as sheet images and GIFs. Open it with File > Export… (Ctrl+E).
Window layout
From left to right the dialog has ① the export list, the selected row's settings and the output preview. Changes go into the selected row right away, and each one can be undone.
⑫ Middle = settings: the selected row's setting sections follow the Format group at the top.
⑬ Right = output preview: the output preview lists each file to be made and its cells. Click a cell to go to its frame.
⑭ Divider: drag it to split the width between the middle and right columns.
Export list
The list has one row for each thing this project exports. The first row is the project's sheet; you can add more rows of the same format with different names or folders (for example, a GIF per tag).
① Export list: click a row to show it in the middle and right columns. Each row shows its file name and kind.
② Add: copies the selected row to the end of the list with _2, _3… added to its name (④ off). Change its format in ⑥.
③ List presets: saves the whole list under a name so you can load it in other projects.
④ On-save checkbox: when on, the row is made again every time you save. A new project's sheet row has it on.
⑤ Red trash button: removes the row. If it made files, you're asked whether to move them to the app trash; Cancel keeps them.
Saving (Ctrl+S) makes every row with ④ on again (see Saving). If two rows would make the same file, you're told the export failed.
Format, name and folder
⑥ Format: PNG, JPG, TGA and BMP make a sheet image with the frames on one picture; GIF, APNG and PNG per frame make an animation. JPG also has a quality setting (1–100%, 90 at first).
⑦ Name and Folder: the file name to make (before the extension; empty = the project name) and its folder. Change them with Change location….
⑧ Game engine: chooses the engine files written with the images: None (default), Unity, Godot 4 or JSON (see Game engine files).
⑨ Prefab, ⑩ Animation and ⑪ Files to be created: shown when Unity is chosen in ⑧.
Export buttons
⑮ Export (blue button): writes only the selected row with the current settings, without saving the .chickxel. A sheet row closes the dialog; an animation row keeps it open.
⑯ Save as…: saves just the same sheet images under a name you choose, apart from the project settings. No Unity settings file is written, and you're asked before overwriting.
Close (Esc) just closes the dialog. Changed settings are already in the project.
Good to know
Switching the project's sheet row to an animation format takes the sheet out of the list and puts an animation row with the same name and folder first.
The window position, size, split and collapsed sections stay the same in other projects.
A long export shows a progress box over the whole window until it finishes; drawing and shortcuts are ignored meanwhile.
Old outputs that are no longer made are cleared by old output cleanup.
When you load a list preset, file names that start with the project name take the new project's name, and folders are relative to the project folder. Loading can be undone.

pages.text:
Read this to put your sheets straight into a game engine such as Unity or Godot. Pick the engine under Game engine in the Format group, and the files that engine reads are written with the images.
Game engine What is written too
None (images only) Images only (the default for new projects).
Unity (.meta) A Unity settings file (.meta) per image, plus the prefab, animations and Sprite Library when turned on.
Godot 4 (SpriteFrames) A SpriteFrames .tres, plus a .tscn when Scene is on.
JSON (Aseprite format, Phaser, PixiJS and more) A .json with the same name for each frame sheet file.
Unity prefab and animations
Choosing Unity shows the two options below (off at first). The files are created in the frame sheet's folder, named after the sheet, and written every time the sheets are exported.
Prefab (layers placed): a Unity object, sheetname.prefab, with the layers in place. It follows the layer tree, and hidden layers go in turned off. Without a layer atlas, it holds one sprite.
Animation (clips and Animator): an animation clip per tag, sheetname_tag.anim, and an Animator that plays them, sheetname.controller. Speed, direction and looping follow the tags, and the first tag plays first.
Files to be created: with an option on, the names of the files to be created are listed (each also gets a .meta).
The prefab, clips and controller are rewritten on every export. To add components or child objects in Unity, do it in a Prefab Variant of this prefab.
Exporting for Godot 4
The Format group with Godot 4 chosen as the game engine: the Scene (.tscn, AnimatedSprite2D) checkbox and the line of files to be created below it
⑰ Scene (.tscn, AnimatedSprite2D)
Choosing Godot 4 (SpriteFrames) writes an animation file, sheetname.tres (SpriteFrames). Put it on an AnimatedSprite2D node in Godot and each tag plays as an animation right away.
⑰ Scene (.tscn, AnimatedSprite2D): when on, a scene with that node, sheetname.tscn, is written too. It keeps pixels sharp and autoplays the first animation.
Exporting JSON
Choosing JSON (Aseprite format, Phaser, PixiJS and more) writes a .json with cell positions, frame durations and tags. It uses the Aseprite format, so web game tools such as Phaser and PixiJS read it as is.
Good to know
Re-exporting keeps Unity's links, so sprites already placed in scenes don't break. Unchanged files aren't rewritten.
The Unity material is Sprite-Lit-Default in URP projects, otherwise Sprites-Default.
Effects applied to a layer together with its children, and top-level normal layers, aren't in the prefab.
Godot 4 and JSON files are made from the frame sheet only, not from the layer atlas.
Turning an option off makes the files it created earlier subject to old output cleanup.

If there is no such row, copy a row with Add and change its format. Save as GIF… in the preview's right-click menu opens the dialog with the first GIF row selected (adding one if there is none).
Settings
① Range: the current tag (at first), all frames or ⑩ a chosen tag. Frames follow the tag's direction (reverse, ping-pong).
② Zoom: 1–10×, keeping pixels crisp (at first, the zoom that makes the result about 256 px).
③ Speed: Original speed (default), Speed multiplier (0.1–10×) or Fixed FPS (1–50). The project's frame durations don't change.
④ Loop: loop forever or play 1–100 times (1 = once).
⑤ Background: transparent or a background color. GIF turns semi-transparent pixels fully transparent or opaque; APNG and PNG per frame keep them with Transparent (alpha kept as is).
Settings are stored per row in the project and can be undone.
Preview and export
⑥ The preview on the right plays at the chosen speed, and ⑦ shows the output size, frame count and duration (and colors for GIF).
⑨ Export writes the file straight to ⑧ the row's name and folder, without a save dialog. A new row targets <project>.gif next to the project (<project>_<tag> for a tag); change it with Change location… in ⑧.
The dialog stays open afterwards, so you can change settings and export again. With the row's on-save checkbox on, the file is made again on every save.
Good to know
GIF rounds frame durations to hundredths of a second and can't go below 20 ms (so Fixed FPS goes up to 50).
With more than 256 colors (255 with transparency), GIF reduces the colors in each frame.
PNG per frame asks before overwriting files with the same names in the folder.
If compositing or writing takes a while, a progress box covers the whole window until it finishes.

Method How
File menu File > Open (.chickxel · image · GIF · video)… (Ctrl+O). Choose 3D models (GLB, glTF, FBX, OBJ) as the file type to see only models.

Format What is drawn Not supported
glTF 2.0 (.glb, .gltf) Shape, colors and textures, transparency and glass, unlit materials, animations Compressed meshes (Draco, meshopt)

Row What it does
① Size The output size (1–2048 px). With the link at the end on (default), the ratio is kept.
② View angle Horizontal (−360 to 360°) circles the model, Vertical (−90 to 90°) looks down from above (90° = straight down), and Roll (−180 to 180°) tilts the image. You can also use the handles in Original.
③ Projection Orthographic keeps sizes equal at any distance, as most game sprites do; Perspective makes near parts larger. Field of view (5–120°) applies to perspective only.
④ Zoom At 100% the model just fits the shorter side (10–1000%). Fit goes back to 100%.
⑤ Light direction Where light comes from (horizontal, vertical), relative to the camera. In a turntable the same side stays lit in every frame.
⑥ Light front/back Moves the light from the front (0°) through the side (90°) to the back (180°). It's the same value as the front/back bar left of Original.
⑦ Brightness Ambient (0–100%) is the brightness of faces the light doesn't reach; Light strength (0–200%) is what the light adds to lit faces.
⑧ Shading steps 0 shades smoothly; 2–16 cut the shading into that many bands, like cel shading.
⑨ Edge smoothing Off (crisp) gives crisp stepped edges; 2×2, 4×4 and 8×8 give smooth ones. Turning off Textures uses only the material base colors.
Color rows below the previews
The Original and Pixel result panes with the Model colors row (orange swatch clicked) and the Colors in this frame row below. Original shows only the beak and feet as they are, with the rest darkened. Marked 10 to 12
⑩ Model colors (the orange of the beak and feet clicked) · ⑪ Where that color is used (the rest darkened, outlined in blue) · ⑫ Colors in this frame
⑩ Model colors: N lists the model's material colors (base colors without light and shade), most used first. Textured parts aren't listed.
⑪ Click a swatch to highlight where that color is used, darkening the rest. Click it again to turn this off.
⑫ Colors in this frame: N lists the colors of the result frame on screen; hover for #RRGGBB.
Changing model colors
The chick drawn in its original colors (left) and with the body feather color changed to chestnut (right). On the right the head and body are chestnut while the wings, beak and comb are unchanged
Left: original colors · Right: body feather color changed to chestnut — 8-direction turntable 64 px (default) values, 30° horizontal, enlarged 4×
Right-click a Model colors swatch and choose Change color… to change it; Back to original and Reset all colors undo changes. Changed colors are used in both the previews and the import.
Only the parts with that color change; other colors stay. A color with transparency draws that part translucent. The model file isn't changed, and opening another model clears the changes.
Shading steps
The same yellow ball drawn with shading steps 0 (left) and 3 (right). The left changes brightness smoothly; the right is cut into three bands
Left: shading steps 0 (smooth) · Right: shading steps 3 — a ball (ball.glb) at 64 px, enlarged 4×
With steps, round surfaces split into a few bands, crisp like hand-drawn shading. Models with only flat faces change little.
Edge smoothing
The chick drawn with edge smoothing off (left) and 4×4 (right). The left has crisp stepped eyes and edges; the right has semi-transparent edges and blended colors
Left: edge smoothing off · Right: 4×4 — 64 px, no-semi-transparency off, enlarged 4×
Off can break up thin parts (eyes, beak); on adds semi-transparent edges and blended colors. When it's on, combine it with No semi-transparency and Colors.

A wooden crate drawn orthographic (left) and in perspective with a 70° field of view (right). On the left parallel edges stay parallel; on the right near edges spread wide
Left: orthographic · Right: perspective (70° field of view) — a wooden crate (crate.obj) at 64 px, enlarged 4×
Use orthographic for sprites placed on a tile grid, and perspective for single illustrations or dramatic icons.

Using Mixamo step by step
On mixamo.com, pick or upload a character and use Download with Format FBX Binary (.fbx) and Skin With Skin.
Download each animation you want with Skin Without Skin. Turn on In Place for loops such as walking and running.
Open the character FBX in Chickxel and pick all the animation FBX files at once with Import… in the import window.
Choose one in the animation list, set it up with a preset (Side view, Character animation and so on) and import.
If you see "ASCII FBX files can't be read", download again from Mixamo with Format FBX Binary. Mixamo animations don't attach to characters from elsewhere, because the bone names don't match.

pages.text:
AI-made "pixel-look" images have uneven cell sizes, blurred edges and hundreds of colors. The Pixelate AI image window turns them into clean pixel art where each source cell becomes one pixel. It takes single images, sprite sheets, animated GIFs, videos and 3D models.
An AI-made source next to the pixelated result
Left: AI-made source (7–8 px cells, blur and JPEG noise) · Right: 49×98 result from the Default preset (enlarged 4×)
Workflow
Load a source: open the window and drop or paste an image.
Run: make candidates with Clean up or Auto optimize.
Pick: compare the candidates' scores and previews and select one.
Touch up (when needed): exclude or pin colors, or change the settings and run again.
Insert: press Apply or Add to new tab.

Step What it does Change it when
0. Optimize criteria Budget (trials, seconds) and scoring rules for Clean up and Auto optimize. Optimization takes too long or stops too early, or the score prefers results that look worse.
Quick settings Gathers often-changed values: output size, Fit cells by row, target colors, Remove background and one palette. You want a given output size, want to turn background removal on or off, or want frames to share colors or not.
1. Background Makes the background transparent (Keep background at first). The source has a solid background that stays in the result, or a white sticker border.
2. Frames Splits a sprite sheet into frames. Frames merge or split in the wrong place.
3. Pixel grid Finds the size of one source "pixel" (the cell size) and the cell boundaries. The result is far too large or small, or cell lines miss the color blocks.
4. Output size Sets the output size from the cell size, a fixed size or a factor. You need a specific size such as 32×32.
5. Cell color Picks one color per cell. Blurred edge colors leak into the result.
6. Palette Merges similar colors into a palette and maps each cell to a palette color. There are too many or too few colors, shading turns into another hue, or you must use a given palette.
7. Cleanup Fixes orphan pixels and holes and fits the outline to 1 px. The outline is thick or broken, or dots such as pupils disappear.
8. Frame consistency Matches pixels that differ slightly from the neighboring frames to reduce flicker. The animation flickers.
Output How the result is inserted: new layer or new document. You want another destination or frame duration.
AI (experimental) Asks the AI chat to touch up the result or rank candidates after applying. You want AI help.

Local cell correction in the 3. Pixel grid step
⑦ Local cell correction, Max shift, Band, Minimum cell size
⑦ Local cell correction (on by default) re-fits the cell lines per band to that band's strong color edges. It follows art that is half a cell off in places.
Settings
Setting Range · default Meaning
Max shift (% of cell) 5–99%, default 35% The farthest a line may move; neighboring cell widths stay within 70–130% of the original.
Band (cells) 1–32 cells, default 2 Width of each band fitted separately. Smaller follows more closely (1 = every row), larger is smoother.
Minimum cell size (px) 1–16 px, default 4 px The average cell size from which correction applies. Lower values also adjust small cells but may follow blur noise.
Good to know
Within a band the lines stay straight, so cells are rectangles; the lines bend where bands change.
The grid stays straight if the average cell is below the minimum or no line moved. The selected-result line shows "Local correction applied to n/m frames" or similar.
With step 3's Optimize on, optimization also tries it on and off with different max shift and band.
Two sharp edges within one cell can't both be matched by one line.
Fit cells by row
Fit cells by row (up to 30%) in Quick settings applies this correction row by row. Turning it on fixes Max shift at 30%, Band at 1 and Minimum cell size at 4 px, and sets the size jitter to 0.
While on, these values, step 3's Optimize check and Optimize grid fit first are disabled. Optimization also leaves the grid alone, along with the settings that affect it (outline lightness, Fit outline to 1 px, sticker border). Turning it off also turns local correction off.

Split a character into child layers of different sizes, such as head, body and legs, under one layer. You export both the combined animation and per-layer sprites. Each layer can hold several sets of outfits or gear (skins), and a skin preset switches several layers at once. You can swap the same combinations in Unity.
The workflow and where each step is explained.
Step What you do Details
1. Build the tree Create a parent layer for a character or a set of gear, then add children or move drawn layers under it. Creating child layers · Nesting and un-nesting layers
2. Draw Draw each layer at its own size in each frame. Effects go on that layer only or on it combined with its children. The layer tree · Drawing (layer with its own size selected) · Layer effects in the tree
3. Layout Move layers by hand or turn on auto layout, and place them per frame if needed. Arranging (empty layer selected) · Changing positions per frame · Auto layout
4. Skins Add another set of art to a layer and choose the skin each layer wears. Skins · Empty skins and duplicating · Switching skins per layer
5. Skin presets Save a skin combination across layers as a preset, switch it at once, and stack presets. Skin settings window · Skin presets
6. Export On save, produce the frame sheet, layer atlas and Sprite Library for Unity. Export: frame sheet and layer atlas · Exporting skins · Unity Sprite Library

Read this when saving a layer-tree character for a game. It can produce two images; turn each on or off in ③ Output.
The two outputs
① Frame sheet: an animation sheet with all layers combined in each frame.
② Layer atlas: one picture (sprite) per layer and frame, collected in one image. If ④ the name is empty, it is <frame sheet name>_parts.
Layer atlas sprites
Only layers in a tree go in, one per drawn frame, in timeline order. Normal layers outside a tree and tilemaps are left out.
Each sprite's Pivot is the layer pivot and its Border is the 9-slice border. Only the layer's own effects are included.
Layout, sorting and cell names follow ⑤ the common settings. Old files no longer produced go to the app trash (Files).
With Unity as the engine, .meta files are written too, and you can produce Prefab (layers placed) (objects nested like the tree), animation clips and a Controller (Export).

Turn on ① Sprite Library (Unity only) in the layer atlas section to create assets for Unity 2D Animation. You switch skins by swapping one asset.
What a library contains
② A default library <layer atlas name>.spriteLib (first skins) plus one per skin preset, <layer atlas name>@<preset>.spriteLib. Only presets containing an exported layer or skin get a file.
Category = layer (same names get 2, 3 …), Label = frame (0, 1 … or idle_0 …).
All libraries share Categories and Labels; only the sprites differ. A preset library uses the preset's skins for its layers and first skins for the rest, so one animation works for every skin.
Cels not drawn in that skin get an empty sprite.
Using it in Unity
Put a Sprite Library component on the top object with the default library.
Give each layer object a Sprite Resolver (Category = layer) and keyframe its Label (frame).
To switch skins, swap the component's asset for a preset library. To switch one layer alone, add another Sprite Library to its object.

Tools
Tool Key What it does
Tile brush B Places the tiles picked in the Tileset panel, in the same arrangement.
Auto tile brush Shift+B Paints with the picked auto tile set; edges follow the neighbors (Auto tiles).
Tile eraser E Drag to erase the visible tile under the pointer; big tiles go whole. With a fixed floor, only that floor.
Tile rectangle R Fills the dragged rectangle with the brush or set.
Tile fill G Fills connected cells that look the same (see Fill).
Tile picker I Picks the visible tile under the pointer, or its auto tile set, into the brush.
Cell select M Selects a rectangle of cells (see Selecting and copying cells).
Mouse and keys
The right button erases.
Hold Alt to pick a tile from the map.
X, Y and Z flip the brush horizontally or vertically and turn it 90°. Turning needs square cells.
Picking and erasing visible images
The picker and cell info use the image visible under the pointer, not just its cell: picking a tree's canopy picks the tree. In position-sorted tilesets the eraser also works on rising images. Rectangle and fill still use cells.
Fill
Tile fill fills connected cells where all visible floors look the same, placing on the target floor. So you can fill just the inside of a wall drawn on another floor. Auto-tiled areas count as one region.
Selecting and copying cells
Select cells and copy them (Ctrl+C) to make them the brush. Cut (Ctrl+X), Delete (Delete) and Select all (Ctrl+A) work on cells too. Paste (Ctrl+V) switches to the tile brush.
Outside the canvas
You can place tiles outside the canvas. When you resize the canvas, outside tiles preview where they will come in, and the grid moves along.

Mark Condition Matches when
Empty Don't care Always.

How a rule is chosen
The first matching rule from the top wins. Put specific rules above broad ones.
If nothing matches, the rule whose conditions miss the least is used.

Join groups

When the reply ends, everything changed in that turn is grouped into one undo step.
How the AI reaches the editor
The AI uses the editor tools through a connection open only on this computer (the MCP server). Each time the app starts it makes a new secret value (token) and rejects requests without it.
There's nothing to set up. The connection details are passed to the CLI on each run (a temporary MCP config), so your Claude and Codex settings stay unchanged.
With Allow external AI apps on in AI > External AI Connection…, other AI apps can use the same tools with their own token (Using other AI apps).

Category What it does Tools
Look at the drawing Reads the open document's size, frames, and layers, views it as an image, or reads exact pixel colors. get_document get_image get_pixels
Generate image → pixelate Draws characters, items and animations (all frames on one sheet) with Codex image generation and converts them to pixel art. Choose the mode and options in Drawing settings in the header. generate_pixel_art
Draw Paints blocks of pixels or single pixels, lines, rectangles, ellipses, fills, clears, and replaces colors. draw_pixels set_pixels draw_shape fill clear replace_color
Frames and animation Adds frames (optionally as copies) or deletes them, and sets frame durations and animation tags. Links cels across frames, unlinks them and recolors links. add_frame delete_frame set_frame_duration add_tag link_cels unlink_cels set_link_color
Layers Adds layers, changes their name, visibility, opacity, and pivot, and picks the frame and layer shown in the editor. add_layer set_layer set_current

Files Creates a new drawing, sets the temporary title of an unsaved new drawing, saves, and opens files (opening and creating are blocked while "Current file only" is on). new_project set_document_title save_project open_file

Ask "link frames 4–8" or "make that link green" and the AI links, unlinks and recolors cels (link_cels, unlink_cels, set_link_color).
Saving and temporary titles
It saves only when asked. When it draws on an unsaved new image, it gives it a short temporary title (even with Current file only on), and asks whether to save before switching to another document.
Good to know: the pixel text the AI reads
When the AI reads exact pixels, the image is sent as text. Each character stands for a color (. is transparent), with x coordinates on top and the y coordinate at the start of each row. For example:
legend:
A = #2B2B3A
B = #C0C0D0
. = transparent
rows:
   001111111111
   890123456789
30|....AAAA....
31|...ABBBBA...
32|..ABBBBBBA..
The AI finds positions from these coordinates, so it misplaces fewer pixels in wide images.

Turning it on
The AI > External AI connection window: the allow checkbox (on) with its info box, the Tools the AI can use column on the left (Open files and Image generation off) and the AI drawing tips column on the right, the connection settings JSON box with the copy button on its right, the How to connect button, and OK and Cancel
① Allow external AI apps and its info box · ② Tools the AI can use · ③ AI drawing tips · ④ Connection settings box and copy button
① Allow external AI apps: turn it on and press OK to start accepting connections. Turning it off cuts off connected apps.
② Tools the AI can use: turns tool groups on or off for that app. Open files and image generation are off at first.
③ AI drawing tips: turns on or off the tips sent to that app. On/off is separate from the chat; edited texts are shared.
④ Connection settings: the settings to paste into the other app. Copy them with the button on the right (Copy connection settings).
② and ③ can be changed only while ① is on. After changing them, restart the app or reconnect its MCP server to see the change.
Registering Chickxel in another AI app
Paste what ④ copies into the app's MCP settings (where it registers outside tools). It looks like this:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "chickxel": {
      "command": "C:\\Users\\me\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Chickxel\\Chickxel.exe",
      "args": ["--mcp"]
    }
  }
}
The Chickxel path is usually %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Chickxel\Chickxel.exe on Windows and /Applications/Chickxel.app/Contents/MacOS/Chickxel.App on macOS. Where to paste it in each app:
App Where to register it
Claude Desktop Add it to mcpServers in claude_desktop_config.json (Settings > Developer > Edit Config), then quit the app completely and start it again.
Claude Code Put it in the project's .mcp.json, or for every folder run claude mcp add --scope user chickxel -- "path to the executable" --mcp.
Cursor Put it in ~/.cursor/mcp.json (one project only: .cursor/mcp.json) and check that chickxel is enabled in the MCP list.
Codex CLI Add the TOML below to ~/.codex/config.toml. Wrap a Windows path in single quotes.
ChatGPT desktop app Uses the same config.toml as Codex CLI (or add it under Settings > MCP servers in the app). Works only in Work or Codex chats.
[mcp_servers.chickxel]
command = 'C:\Users\me\AppData\Local\Programs\Chickxel\Chickxel.exe'
args = ["--mcp"]
tool_timeout_sec = 3600
tool_timeout_sec = 3600 keeps long tools such as image generation from being cut off at 60 seconds.
Once registered, the app lists the chickxel tools. Try asking it to "add a 1px white outline to the open image".

pages.text:
Read this to see how an external AI app differs from AI chat, and what to check when it won't connect.
How it works
The app starts Chickxel as a connection-only process with no window (Chickxel --mcp).
Chickxel runs only the tools you allowed, and the canvas changes right away.
Long tools such as image generation send progress notes while you wait.
You don't need to restart the app after restarting Chickxel.
Differences from AI chat
Check this table when something behaves differently from AI chat.
Item AI chat External AI connection
Connection Chickxel starts the CLI. The app starts Chickxel --mcp (register once).
Usage Your Claude or ChatGPT subscription That app's plan, plus your Codex quota for image generation.
Undo One reply is one step (Undoing) One tool call is one step ("AI: tool name")
AI questions A question card (While the AI works) Asked in the app's conversation (no ask_user).
Opening files Opens files with open_file. Only with Open files turned on (off at first)
Image generation Follows the drawing mode in drawing settings. Only when turned on. When it's done, the Pixelate AI images window opens right away.
Current file only Turned on with the chat button (Limiting what the AI can edit). Not used.
Locked layers Never touched. The same.
Drawing rules Given as the system prompt (with the tips that are on). Sent the same rules and enabled tips on connecting (some apps may ignore them).
Where you see it Tool lines and result pictures in the chat window The app's conversation; Chickxel shows only canvas changes and the connection indicator.
Safety
The connection is open only on this computer and needs a secret value (token) that is new each time Chickxel starts.
<settings folder>/Chickxel/mcp-external.json, which holds the token, exists only while the connection is on. Other programs under your account can use it to connect, so turn the connection off when you don't need it.
The AI saves only when asked and never touches locked layers.
Images and document details the app looks at go to that app's model.
If it doesn't connect
Symptom Fix
The app gets "Chickxel isn't running or its external AI connection is off" Start Chickxel and check that Allow external AI apps is on. The app then continues without a restart.
The app has no chickxel tools Check the config file's location and the JSON's commas and brackets, then restart the app. If you moved Chickxel, copy the connection settings again.
open_file or generate_pixel_art is missing or refused as "not available over the external AI connection" Turn that group on in Tools the AI can use and reconnect. ask_user is never available externally.
Image generation fails with "Couldn't read subject_image as a PNG image" The app can't pass the image as a base64 PNG without a data: prefix. Describe the subject in words instead.

Command Default key What it does

Cut Ctrl+X Cuts the selection to the clipboard.
Copy Ctrl+C Copies the selection, or the whole frame if nothing is selected.

Command Default key What it does
Drop selection Enter Drops pasted or moved pixels in place. While transforming, applies the transform.
Deselect (canvas) Esc Cancels a transform or size mode, otherwise removes the selection.
Move 1px Ctrl+Shift+Left Ctrl+Shift+Right Up Down Moves the selection (with the Move tool, the cel's pixels) by 1 pixel.
Move 8px Shift+Left Shift+Right Shift+Up Shift+Down Moves the same thing by 8 pixels.
Good to know
Undo works per stroke, 1000 steps by default. You can raise it to 10000 in Preferences.
For sideways moves add Ctrl+Shift. Plain ←→ go to the previous and next frame.
In a moving mode (Move tool, transform, canvas size, arranging an empty layer's children), plain ←→ move too after you click the canvas.

pages.text:
To make a new language, export the translation CSV, add a language column, translate it and add the file back. Edit the CSV in a spreadsheet such as Excel or Google Sheets. You can add a partial translation; empty cells show English.
Exporting and translating
The Language part of the General tab in Preferences: the Display language list, the Export translation CSV…, Add language from CSV… and Open language folder buttons and the note
① Export translation CSV… · ② Add language from CSV…
Save a CSV file with ① Export translation CSV… in Preferences. You can open it in Excel, Google Sheets and so on.
The first row is key,ko,en and the second row is #name,한국어,English. Add a new column at the far right with the language code in the first row (e.g. ja) and the language name in the second row (e.g. 日本語).
Translate the text in that column. Braces such as {0} and {name} are placeholders for values, so keep them as they are (you may change their order).
CSV layout
Row Content
First row key and the language codes (key,ko,en,…). A language code uses letters, digits, - and _, up to 32 characters.
Second row #name and the name shown in the list for each language (#name,한국어,English,…)
Other rows The text key (<table>.<key>, e.g. UiStrings.Language_Label) and the text for each language. Don't change the keys.
The exported file is comma-separated UTF-8. Importing reads comma, semicolon and tab separators, so it's fine if Excel saves with semicolons. One file can contain several language columns.
Adding and applying it
The Display language list open after adding a CSV with a Japanese column: 日本語 (ja) appears below 한국어 and English, with the import result below
③ The language added from the CSV (e.g. 日本語 (ja)); the number of imported strings is shown below the list
Choose the file with ② Add language from CSV… and it appears in the ③ language list. If you added just one new language, it is selected for you. Click OK and restart to apply it.
The number of strings added for each language appears below the list ("{name} ({code}): added {count} strings.").
Columns that aren't valid language codes are skipped and keys Chickxel doesn't have are ignored; the counts are reported.
Adding the same language code again overwrites it. Added languages are saved as <settings folder>/Chickxel/Languages/<language code>.csv.

pages.text:
Chickxel terms used in this guide and what they mean. Click a term to open the page that explains it. In the guide text, the first mention of a term on each page links to the same place.
Term Meaning
9-slice A Unity sprite border that splits an image into nine parts so its corners stay crisp when stretched.
account level (level badge, level chip) Your Chickxel account's level, which rises with the XP you earn by sharing and shows as an Lv badge next to your name.
active palette The palette you last clicked or edited; Edit-menu and AI palette tools use it.
Add range The effect range given to effects newly added in the effects dialog.
AI chat The window where you ask Claude or Codex to edit the drawing.
AI drawing tips (drawing tips) Per-task tips given to the AI in advance so rough requests still come out as good pixel art; each can be turned on or off and edited.
AI references (reference library) A library of images, notes and rules on your computer that the AI looks through before drawing.
AI Status window (AI Status and Settings) The window that checks CLI installation, version, sign-in and MCP connection, and installs or signs in.
AI tools (MCP tools) The editor functions Chickxel exposes over MCP for the AI to read and edit the image.
allowing scripts to run (allowed to run) Deciding that a script effect you haven't seen before may run on this computer.
animated effect (animated effects) An effect that changes over its effect range (flash, shake, explode and so on).
animated tile (animated tiles) A tile that cycles through several images at a set time per image.
app trash Chickxel's own trash that keeps deleted files and old export outputs for a while (separate from the Windows or macOS trash; File > View app trash…).
apply effect permanently (apply permanently, applied permanently) Bakes an effect into the cel pixels and removes it from the effect list.
Apply to frames (frame range) A brush tool setting that applies a stroke to the other frames in a chosen range at the same spot as on the current frame.
Apply to layers An eraser setting that applies the stroke at the same spot to other layers in the same frame (above, below, all or selected layers) as well as the current one.
Asset Manager The window for installing, importing and publishing assets such as effects and gradients.
auto layout A layer setting that lines its direct children up by size and re-lines them up whenever the children change.
Auto optimize Searches each checked preset for the highest-scoring values of the steps that have Optimize on.
auto tile rule (auto tile rules) One entry of an auto tile set: conditions on the 8 neighbors plus the tiles to place. Rules are tried from the top.
auto tile set (auto tile sets, auto tiles, auto tile) A set of rules that places tiles with the right edge shape by looking at the 8 neighbors of each cell.
autosave Saves automatically after a short pause.
base position The layer position shared by all frames; per-frame distances are added to it.
big tile (big tiles) A tile whose footprint is larger than 1×1; it replaces every tile it overlaps on the same floor.
brush shape (brush size) The shape (square, circle, diamond) and size (1–32) that brush tools such as the pencil and eraser paint at once.
built-in tileset The Sandbox surface & caves and Top-down village & water tilesets shipped with the app; projects receive copies.
candidate tile (candidate row) A tile in the Pixelate window showing one preset's result and score; click to select it, double-click to apply it.
canvas The central area where you view the current frame and draw.
canvas pivot The canvas's own pivot used for sheet and Unity exports; with a representative layer it follows that layer's pivot.
canvas size mode A mode for setting the new canvas size and image position directly on the canvas.
cel (cels) The drawing of one layer in one frame — a single timeline cell.
cel shading Shading that cuts brightness into a few flat bands.
cell name (cell names) The sprite name of each sheet cell (by frame number or by tag).
Chickxel account The chickxel.com account used for gallery and asset uploads (sign in with Google, GitHub or Discord).
child layer (child layers) A layer nested under another layer. It has its own size and position and is drawn above its parent's picture.
Choose help on screen (help picker) Press F1, then click a button or panel on screen to open its guide page.
Claude Code Anthropic's command-line AI tool. Signed in with a Claude subscription, it powers the Claude tab of AI chat.
Clean up lines (line cleanup) An Edit menu command that finds the outlines and inner lines of the current layer and redraws them as clean 1 px lines and arcs with even steps.
clipping (clip to effect above) A setting that applies an effect only to the pixels made by the effect above it.
Codex CLI OpenAI's command-line AI tool. Signed in with a ChatGPT subscription, it powers the Codex tab and image generation.
color decision The row in the enlarged view that shows how one pixel's color was decided at each step.
color distance How closeness between two colors is measured (OKLCh hue-weighted, CIEDE2000, OKLab), used when cells pick palette colors.
color picker The panel that sets the color being edited with a square, honeycomb, wheel or sliders.
color space The color model used to blend a smooth gradient (RGB, HSL, OKLab, OKLCH).
Contiguous only A setting that limits fill and the magic wand to the area connected to the clicked pixel.
convert to palette colors Replaces the image's colors with the nearest palette colors.
copy images only (images-only copy, images-only copies) Copies timeline cels or frames as images only without their link groups.
Current file only A chat toggle that limits the AI to the image open when you send.
curve pen (Curve Pen) A drawing tool that builds and adjusts a curve (Bézier) path from anchor points and handles, then paints it as a clean 1 px line with even steps.
display language The language of menus, windows and messages; changing it takes effect after a restart.
dithering Mixing two colors in a dot pattern so they read as an in-between color; used by the dithering tool, gradients and palette conversion.
document tab (document tabs) A tab above the canvas for each open document.
Dodge/burn (Lighten/darken) A tool that rubs painted pixels lighter (left button) or darker (right button).
Draw pixels directly A drawing mode where the AI places pixels one by one with the pixel tools.
Drawing settings (drawing settings) The chat panel that sets the drawing mode and generation options.
easing How an animated effect speeds up and slows down over its range.
Effect Maker The window for writing, previewing and publishing script effects.
effect padding The space an effect reserves outside the image to draw in (outline thickness, shadow offset and so on).
effect preset (effect presets) Several effects and their values saved together under a name.
effect range (effect ranges) The frames an effect applies to: all frames or a start–end frame.
effect row (effect rows, effect box) The row each effect gets under its layer in the timeline, with a box showing its range.
effects dialog The dialog for adding effects to one layer, changing their order, settings and ranges, and previewing them.
empty layer (empty layers) A parent layer that only holds its children and has no picture of its own (created with New empty layer).
empty layer view The canvas state with an empty layer selected, where you see the frame composite and drag the child layers into place.
end chick The chick shown on the last frame of a transform effect's preview.
enlarged preview A resizable window that plays the preview enlarged.
eraser A tool that erases pixels to transparent (or by a strength and channels).
error log (error logs) Files describing unexpected errors; the latest 20 are kept in Logs in the settings folder.
excluded color (excluded colors) Removing one color from the selected result, replacing its pixels with the nearest remaining color.
export cell name (export cell names, cell naming rule) The name of a cell (Unity sprite) in an exported sheet, set per frame or generated by the naming rule.
Export dialog The dialog that exports your picture as sheet images, GIFs, game engine files and more.
export on save The checkbox on each export list row; when on, that row's outputs are made whenever you save. The sheet row of a new project has it on.
export path encryption Writing a project file's export folder and names locked with this install's own key (local-path-key.bin), so others can't see your folder paths.
export preset (export presets) Named export settings you can reuse in other projects.
Extend frames An effects dialog setting that adds frames to an effect's range to create animation frames.
external AI connection A setting that lets other AI apps use the running Chickxel's editor tools through Chickxel --mcp.
eyedropper A tool that picks a canvas color into the primary or secondary color.
fast path The execution path that converts and compiles a script's source to run it fast.
ffmpeg An external program used to open videos, AVIF and HEIC files; it isn't bundled with Chickxel and must be installed separately.
Fidelity The largest score term, measuring how closely the result matches the background-removed source cells.
file association The OS registration that makes double-clicking a .chickxel in Explorer or Finder open Chickxel.
file browser The left panel that shows a folder's images as thumbnails and opens them.
first skin (base skin) The skin at the front of a layer's skin list; it uses the plain cell names in the layer atlas.
Fit cells by row A Quick setting that starts from a uniform grid, fits cell boundaries per row and column to the source's color edges within 30%, and keeps the grid fixed during optimization.
Fit outline to 1 px How a thick outer outline becomes 1 px: By shrinking, Thin outline only, Redraw as vector or Off.
fit to window Switches to the largest zoom that fits the whole image in the canvas area.
floating selection Selected pixels that were lifted or pasted and not yet dropped.
footprint (footprints) The number of cells (width × height) a tile covers on the map; its image may be larger.
frame (frames) One picture of the animation: a timeline column with its own duration (ms).
frame duration How long one frame is shown (ms).
frame header (frame headers) The frame number cell in the timeline's top row; click it to select the frame.
frame sheet A PNG with every frame laid out in a grid.
frame split The step that splits a source with several frames into one frame each.
Generate image → pixelate A drawing mode that makes a picture with Codex image generation and converts it to pixel art.
GIF animation (animated PNG) An Export dialog format that makes a single animation file (GIF or APNG) for sharing.
gradient pencil A pencil that paints along the stroke in gradient colors.
gradient preset (gradient presets) A gradient saved under a name with its stops, interpolation, color space and dithering.
gradient stop (color stop, opacity stop) A point on the gradient bar that sets which color (or opacity) sits at which position.
gradient tool A tool that paints a linear gradient by dragging.
grid detection Finding how many source pixels make one "pixel" and where the cell boundaries are.
guide window The in-app window for searching and browsing this guide (Help > Guide…).
hue shift A shading method that turns the hue toward yellow when lightening and toward blue/purple when darkening (the default lighten/darken mode).
image chip (image chips) The marker for an attached image inside the message text: a thumbnail and a #number.
image markup window A window where you mark the spots to fix on an image in the chat with lines and numbered comments and send it to the AI.
Import 3D model The window that draws a 3D model into pixel-art frames after you set its size, angle, light, outlines and frames.
Import Settings The Unity Texture Importer settings written to the .meta file.
Import video The window that extracts a video into frames after you set the range, frame rate and size.
info box (info boxes, info badge, info badges) The small rounded square with an i. Hover or click it to show a longer explanation; click again to close it.
join group (join groups) A name that makes auto tile sets sharing it connect without an edge, even on different floors.
keep the end look Keeps an animated effect's final appearance on frames after its range.
keyboard shortcut (keyboard shortcuts) Keys that run a command directly; you can change them in Preferences.
language folder The Languages folder in the settings folder where added languages and edited text are stored.
lasso select (lasso) A selection tool that selects the inside of an outline you draw.
layer (layers) One sheet you paint on. It is a timeline row; upper layers cover lower ones.
layer atlas A PNG that packs the drawings of the layers in the layer tree, one cell per layer × frame.
layer colors The colors used in every frame of the current layer, most used first.
layer effect (layer effects) Effects such as outline, shadow or flash that are layered on without changing the pixels.
layer pivot (layer pivots) The pivot each layer has (measured against the canvas for a normal layer, against its own area for a layer with its own size); that layer's effects, transform rotation center, symmetry axis and layer atlas sprite use it.
layer tree The structure formed by nesting layers under other layers as children, several levels deep.
level reward (level rewards) A profile decoration unlocked at each level from 2 to 100 (title, level badge, frame, effect, card or nickname effect); every slot is on Auto by default.
linked cels (cel link) A link that makes several cels share one drawing; editing one changes them all.
linked copy (linked copies) Copying timeline cels together with their link groups, so cels pasted into the same row join the original group.
local cell correction Re-fits the image-wide cell lines band by band to the real color edges.
locked layer (locked layers) A layer locked with the timeline padlock so that drawing and AI edits can't change it.
magic wand A selection tool that selects the area of similar color around the click (same settings as Fill).
magic wand preview A magic wand feature that tints blue the pixels a click under the mouse would select, and red the ones that would leave the selection.
MCP Model Context Protocol, the connection the AI CLI uses to call Chickxel's editor tools.
merge files Combines several images selected in the file browser into one .chickxel.
meta file (meta files) The Unity settings file (.meta) next to an exported image, holding sprite cells, pivots and the guid.
middle fill Chooses whether the middle is stretched (Stretch) or its pattern repeated (Tile) when stretching with 9-slice.
Mixamo Adobe's free web service that rigs humanoid 3D characters and lets you download animations for them.
move pivot along Moves the center (pivot) of later effects by as much as a moving effect moved the image.
Move tool The tool that moves the selection or the whole cel; Ctrl turns any tool into it while held.
Movement test A window (F5) where you move a character as in a top-down or platformer game using its tag animations.
my assets Assets made on this computer or published with your account; you edit them in place.
named group there A condition matching a neighboring auto tile on any floor whose join group matches the rule’s Group field.
nearest neighbor A scaling and rotation method that uses the nearest original pixel without blending colors.
New project dialog The dialog that creates a new document from a canvas size and a background setting.
number field (number fields) A field you change by clicking to type, using the up/down buttons at its right end, or picking from its right-click list.
official effect (official effects) The 23 script effects the app installs by default (Outline, Shadow, Hit flash and so on).
onion skin A view option that overlays neighboring frames translucently.
Optimize criteria The per-preset budget (trials, seconds) and scoring rules for Clean up and Auto optimize.
palette A list of colors to paint with. You can stack several and switch between them.
palette web (Lospec) A window for browsing and importing palettes from lospec.com.
parent layer (parent layers) A layer that has child layers. Hiding, locking, opacity and moving apply to its children as well.
peek previous frame Shows the previous frame on the canvas while the key is held.
pencil The basic drawing tool that paints pixels in the brush shape.
per-frame pivot A pivot (and for a layer with its own size, position) kept separately from a given frame to the end with 'From current frame on'.
per-frame position (per-frame positions) A layer placement that differs from the base position in a particular frame.
pick card The card in the tool options showing the tile or auto tile set about to be placed and its target floor.
pick from screen A color popup button that picks a color anywhere on the screen, other apps included.
ping-pong A tag direction that plays to the end and back.
pinned color (pinned colors) A color picked from a source cell and added to the result palette; only pixels closer to it change.
pivot The reference point for rotation and placement, exported as the Unity sprite pivot.
Pivot tool The tool for setting the pivot by dragging on the canvas or with buttons and numbers.
pixel font (pixel fonts) A font drawn on a pixel grid; Galmuri, Unifont and others come with the app.
pixel grid A view option that outlines every pixel when zoomed in.
pixel perfect An option that removes the doubled L-shaped pixels at stair corners when drawing at size 1, leaving a one-pixel line.
Pixel steps A setting that joins the pixels of shape lines and curves, or of pencil, gradient pencil and eraser strokes, diagonally (Diagonal) or only sideways and up/down (Orthogonal); the Shape tool and the pencil remember it separately.
Pixelate AI image (Pixelate) The window that turns AI-made or large images into clean pixel art.
pixels outside the canvas Pixels pushed past the canvas edge. They are kept and can be brought back.
Prefer shade family Prefers a palette color of the cell's own hue family over a different hue of similar lightness.
preset parameter (preset parameters) A value in an effect preset that changes settings of several effects inside it together.
preview board The 12×9 board in the auto tile set editor for trying the set you are editing; it isn't saved.
preview chick The 20 numbered chick pictures that effect and preset previews apply the effect to.
preview position and pivot Declaration values that move the end chick and each frame's pivot in effect previews.
preview scene A small drawing used with the chick to preview effects that read other layers.
preview tab A green-tinted tab that plays the document being edited, enlarged, in the other pane.
primary color (Primary) The color painted with the left mouse button.
project file (project files) The .chickxel file that holds everything you edit: layers, frames, effects, export settings and more.
publish online The window that publishes one of your assets to the Store and chickxel.com with your Chickxel account.
question card The card with options that appears above the input box when the AI asks you to decide.
received assets (received asset) Assets by others from the Store or files; copy one to My assets to change it.
recent colors The last 16 colors you painted with, newest first.
recent files The list of the last 10 opened or saved files, in the File menu and on the start screen.
recovery file (recovery files) A .chickxel saved separately for an unsaved document when an error forces the app to quit.
Replace color brush (color replace brush) A brush that, where you rub, changes only the color of the pixel where the stroke started.
representative layer The layer whose pivot the canvas pivot follows in every frame (crown before its name).
resampling How rotated or scaled pixels take their colors from the original (RotSprite / Nearest).
Revert to saved A command that discards unsaved edits and rereads the file from disk.
Right button = eraser An option that makes the right button of the pencil, gradient pencil, shape and fill tools erase instead of using the secondary color.
rotation center The point transform mode and Transform whole layer rotate around; it starts at the current layer's pivot.
RotSprite A pixel-art rotation method that samples an 8× enlarged copy so rotated lines break less (no new colors).
score term (score breakdown) The terms, such as Fidelity and 1-px outline, and their weights that make up a candidate's 0–100 score.
script API The declaration, settings, img, ctx and other names and rules used in a script effect's source.
script effect (script effects) An effect written in JavaScript.
secondary color (Secondary) The color painted with the right mouse button (it erases when Right button = eraser is on).
seed A number that fixes the look of a random effect; the same seed always gives the same look.
sel-out Drawing an outline with darkened versions of the colors beneath it instead of one color.
selection The area chosen with a selection tool; painting, erasing and moving stay inside it.
settings folder (app settings folder) The Chickxel folder holding preferences, undo history, the app trash and logs (%AppData%\Chickxel on Windows).
shape pen (shape set) A drawing tool that stamps small pictures (leaves, flowers, sparkles, chick characters and more) from the chosen set. Eight built-in sets come with it; you can make your own sets, edit them on the canvas, and get or publish sets in the Store.
Shape tool A tool that drags out 11 shapes such as lines, curves, rectangles, ellipses and stars.
show effects on canvas A view option that decides whether layer effects are shown on the editing canvas.
skin (skins) One set of drawings for a layer (outfit, body type and so on). Each layer can keep several and swap between them.
skin chip (skin chips) The small label after the timeline name of a layer with more than one skin, showing its current skin; click it for the skin list and Skin settings….
skin preset (skin presets) A named set of skins, one per layer, for several layers. Applying it changes only the layers it contains.
skin row The row below the preview where you pick a skin preset and each layer's skin.
Skin settings window The window that shows the skin presets and each layer's skins as cards for editing.
something there An auto tile condition (orange triangle) that matches when the neighbor holds the same group or any tile on the chosen floors.
split view The canvas divided into left and right panes showing two documents.
Sprite Library The .spriteLib asset Unity uses to swap skins.
start screen The screen shown with no document open, where you choose a folder, recent file or Unity Hub project.
status bar The bottom line showing coordinates, color, size and save state.
style rules The pixel-art rules the AI follows when drawing: the built-in rules plus your own rules.md.
symmetry drawing (horizontal symmetry, vertical symmetry) An option that also draws on the opposite side of the canvas center (or pivot) axis.
tag (tags) A named frame range that groups an animation (for example idle or run).
target colors A color count above which (or, when Strict, below which) the score is reduced.
temporary MCP config The MCP server address and token Chickxel passes straight to the CLI on each run, separate from your CLI settings.
text box A text area dragged out with the Text tool; lines wrap within its width.
the Store (Store tab) The Asset Manager tab for finding and installing effects, gradients and shape pen sets published on chickxel.com.
tile floor (tile floors) An ordered set of cells inside a tilemap layer; the same floor overwrites, different floors stack.
tile grid A view option that draws a line every tile of the chosen size.
tile tools (tile brush, auto tile brush) The tools used on tilemap layers instead of the pixel tools: tile brush, auto tile brush, eraser, rectangle, fill, picker and cell select.
tiled mode A view option that repeats the image around itself to check seamless patterns.
tilemap layer (tilemap layers) A layer that builds a map by placing tileset tiles on a grid of cells; every frame uses the same map.
tileset (tilesets) A collection of tiles, floors and auto tile sets for tilemap layers, stored as a copy in the project.
tileset file (tileset files) A .chickxel-tileset file holding one tileset, so several projects can share it.
Tileset panel The panel on the left, shown for tilemap layers, where you pick tiles and auto tile sets to place.
Tileset settings window The window that edits one tileset's tiles, floors, auto tile sets, file and view; changes apply right away.
timeline The bottom panel that shows frames (columns) and layers (rows) as cels.
tolerance How different a color may be and still count as the same for fill and magic wand.
tool line (tool lines) A chat line showing an editor tool the AI called, its result and how long it took.
Tool options (tool options) The right-dock panel where you change the current tool's settings.
toolbar The vertical bar on the far left for picking tools.
top bar The bar below the menus with the tool name, view options and zoom.
transform mode A mode for rotating, scaling and moving the selected pixels with handles.
transform whole layer A mode that rotates, scales, moves and distorts every frame of one layer (every skin of a part) together with one orange box.
translation CSV A spreadsheet file with every UI string as a key and one column per language; add a column to make a new language.
turntable (turntables) A frame mode that turns a 3D model one full circle and draws one image per evenly spaced direction, used for 8-direction sprites.
tutorial (tutorials) An in-app guide that teaches a feature step by step with the spot to use lit up on screen and a bubble next to it (Help > Tutorial…).
undo history Undo steps that survive closing and reopening a file.
Undo this step The button under an AI reply that undoes everything that reply changed.
update dialog (automatic update) The dialog that shows a new version and its changes, then downloads, installs and restarts.
Upload to gallery The window that uploads a picture to the chickxel.com gallery.
Use palette colors only A drawing setting that snaps the colors the AI paints to the nearest color in the current palette.
Use the source outline A 7. Cleanup setting that makes Fit outline to 1 px peel only the cells detected as outline on the source.
wrap around A Move tool option that brings pixels pushed off one side back on the other side.
XP Points from gallery pictures, shared assets, likes, daily check-ins and app time that raise your account level.
zoom level How much the canvas is magnified (1–64×, whole steps).
